title: an identifier may begin with a Unicode letter
rule: An identifier begins with a Unicode letter or underscore (`_`) and continues with letters, digits, or underscores.

title: identifiers are case-sensitive
rule: Identifiers are case-sensitive: `Foo`, `foo`, and `FOO` are distinct.

title: string and String name the same type
rule: The lowercase keyword `string` and the standard-library type name `String` name the same type — they are interchangeable in source.

title: the bare underscore cannot be declared as a local's name
rule: The bare underscore `_` is not an identifier — never declarable and never readable as a name; `var _ := e;` is a compile error.

title: an identifier merely containing an underscore is ordinary
rule: Identifiers merely containing underscores (`_camelCase`, `snake_case`, `_f`) are ordinary identifiers; only the bare single-character token is reserved.

title: a parameter cannot be named the bare underscore
rule: The bare underscore `_` is never declarable as a name; every declaration named `_` — including a method parameter — is a compile error naming the sanctioned forms (§17.13).

title: a named parameter is an ordinary declaration
rule: An identifier merely containing an underscore is ordinary; a properly named parameter is unaffected by the discard rule.

title: a bare underscore cannot be read as a value
rule: The bare underscore is never readable as a name; a bare `_` in expression position is a compile error — `_` is not a value, so no such read can resolve (§17.13).

title: reading an ordinary local in expression position is legal
rule: A bare underscore cannot be read as a value; an ordinary literal read in the same position is unaffected.

title: a reserved keyword cannot be used as an identifier
rule: Reserved words may not be used as identifiers, except for the contextual keywords listed in Appendix B which have meaning only in specific syntactic positions.

title: an identifier that merely resembles a keyword is legal
rule: Reserved words may not be used as identifiers; a spelling that is not itself a reserved word is unaffected.

title: a contextual keyword is an ordinary identifier outside its position
rule: Contextual keywords have meaning only in specific syntactic positions; used elsewhere they are ordinary identifiers.

title: Exception is a PascalCase name, not a keyword
rule: Type identifiers like `Object`, `Array`, and `Exception` are not keywords; they are PascalCase names defined in the standard library.

title: block comments do not nest
rule: `/* ... */` — block comment, does not nest.

title: a method's end label matching its name is accepted
rule: Named constructs — method bodies included — take the identifier as the optional end label: `end methodName;`.

title: a method's end label that mismatches its name is rejected
rule: The optional label is the identifier: `end methodName;`. A mismatch is a compile error.

title: a constructor closed with the wrong introducing keyword is rejected
rule: Keyword-labelled constructs are labelled by the keyword that introduced the block (`end constructor;`, `end destructor;`); a label that does not match the construct's introducing keyword is a compile error.

title: a constructor closed with its own introducing keyword is accepted
rule: Keyword-labelled constructs are labelled by the keyword that introduced the block: `end constructor;`.

title: a labeled loop closed with the unlabeled keyword form is rejected
rule: A loop carrying a loop label is a named construct; the keyword closer (`end for;`) is rejected once the loop is labeled.

title: a labeled loop closed with its own label is accepted
rule: A loop carrying a loop label is a named construct; its closer is `end label;` or the unlabelled `end;`.

title: a nested loop cannot reuse an enclosing loop's label
rule: A loop label duplicates no loop label in scope at its declaration (Appendix C.5).

title: a nested loop with a distinct label is accepted
rule: A loop label duplicates no loop label in scope at its declaration; a distinct inner label is unaffected.

title: a dotted module name is one unnested identifier
rule: A module name is a single identifier or a sequence of identifiers separated by dots. The dotted form is a single name; it does not establish nesting.

title: an import alias is usable as a type qualifier
rule: An import may bind a file-scoped alias: `import BankingApp.Transactions as Tx;` — thereafter `Tx.Ledger` names that module's public `Ledger`.

title: naming a type requires importing its declaring module
rule: All other library modules require explicit `import` — importing `System.Threading` is required to name `CancellationTokenSource`.

title: naming a type is admitted once its module is imported
rule: All other library modules require explicit `import`; once imported, naming the type is admitted.

title: a duplicate plain import of the same module is idempotent
rule: A duplicate plain `import` of a module already imported in the same file is idempotent: the later occurrence adds nothing and is not diagnosed.

title: a current-module declaration shadows a same-named auto-imported name
rule: A declaration in the current module shadows any same-named import for bare-name purposes (the import stays reachable by qualifier) — the same shadowing already specified for auto-imported names.

title: an import alias cannot collide with a type declared in the module
rule: An alias may not collide with another alias, an imported module's name segment in qualifier position, a type declared in the file's module, or an unambiguously imported public bare name.

title: an alias with no colliding declaration is accepted
rule: An alias may not collide with a type declared in the file's module; a distinctly-named type is unaffected.

title: several always-available names are usable with no import
rule: The following names are visible in every source file without import — including `System`'s `Console`, `System.Text`'s `StringBuilder`, and `System.Collections.Generic`'s `Array<T>`.

title: a non-auto stdlib type is not visible without its import
rule: All other library modules require explicit `import`. `CancellationTokenSource` is NOT auto — it needs `import System.Threading;`.

title: importing System.Threading makes CancellationTokenSource visible
rule: All other library modules require explicit `import`. `CancellationTokenSource` needs `import System.Threading;` — supplying it makes the name resolve and the file compile.

title: a user module's export collides with an auto-imported bare name
rule: A user module exporting one of the §2.3 always-available bare names makes the bare name ambiguous in a file importing both, and no opt-out exists.

title: qualifying the colliding name resolves the ambiguity
rule: A user module exporting an always-available bare name makes the bare name ambiguous; qualification (the module name or an alias, §2.2) is the remedy — no opt-out exists, but qualifying reaches the intended declaration.

title: naming Ptr<T> requires importing System.Interop
rule: `System.Interop` — `Ptr<T>` and the `Interop` intrinsics — is deliberately not auto-imported, so *naming* `Ptr<T>` or `Interop` requires the `import System.Interop;` line.

title: importing System.Interop makes Ptr<T> nameable
rule: `System.Interop` — `Ptr<T>` and the `Interop` intrinsics — is deliberately not auto-imported, so *naming* `Ptr<T>` requires the `import System.Interop;` line; supplying it makes the name resolve.

title: a chain head resolves to a reachable type over a same-named member
rule: Chain head — name followed by `.`: enclosing-type members rank last, after aliases — a reachable type outranks a same-named member. No warning fires because the member's declared type is the resolved type (the `property Color: Color` idiom).

title: a bare value read resolves to a same-named member over a type
rule: Bare value read: enclosing-type members rank between local scope and module declarations — a member outranks a same-named top-level type.

title: chain head resolving to a type warns when the shadowed member's declared type differs
rule: Warning row — chain head resolves to a type while a same-named accessible member exists: warn, *unless* the member's declared type is the resolved type (or an instantiation of the resolved generic). `Status` the member is declared `string`, not `Status` the type, so the carve-out does not apply.

title: a dotted prefix matching no import is an error at the leftmost segment
rule: Otherwise, match the longest dotted prefix of the chain against an imported module's full name. A prefix matching *no* import is an error at `A` (naming the unresolved segment).

title: the longest dotted prefix matching an imported module's full name resolves the chain
rule: Otherwise, match the longest dotted prefix of the chain against an imported module's full name. The remainder then resolves against that module's public declarations. `Data.Store` is the imported module's full (dotted) name; `Item` is the remainder.

title: a type named A shadows an imported module-name prefix A for chain purposes
rule: Consequences worth stating — a type named `A` in scope **shadows** a module-name prefix `A.…` for chain purposes (the compiler warns when both readings exist). `Data` the locally-declared type wins over `Data` the imported module's prefix.

title: an unimported module's presence in the build does not satisfy rule 2's prefix match
rule: Match the longest dotted prefix of the chain against an *imported* module's full name. A prefix matching no import is an error at `A`, even when a module of that name is known to the build — `Data.Store` is compiled as part of this build but never `import`ed by this file, so `Data` does not resolve.

title: a module cannot import itself
rule: An `import` naming the enclosing file's own module is rejected ("a module cannot import itself").

title: importing a distinct module is accepted
rule: An `import` naming the enclosing file's own module is rejected; importing a distinct module is unaffected.

title: declaring an implementation-provided module name is a build error
rule: The standard-library modules are implicit members of every build's artifact set; they participate in duplicate-name detection — a root compilation declaring a module name the implementation provides (`module System;`, `module System.Threading;`, …) is the rule-3 build error.

title: the root compilation may not declare a dependency's module name
rule: A build whose artifact set — the root compilation plus the dependency closure — contains two distinct artifacts declaring the same module name, or a dependency artifact declaring a module name the root compilation also declares, is ill-formed; the diagnostic names both origins.

title: a root module name distinct from every dependency is accepted
rule: A build's artifact set is ill-formed only when two distinct artifacts declare the same module name; a distinct root module name alongside a dependency is unaffected.

title: an aliased import of the file's own module is still a self-import
rule: An `import` naming the enclosing file's own module is rejected ("a module cannot import itself"); the self-loop is not a cycle, it is a mistake. An `as` alias renames the binding, it does not change which module is named.

title: an implementation-provided module resolves with no artifact supplied
rule: The standard-library modules are provided by the implementation, not by any presented artifact: implicit members of every build's artifact set, exempt from §2.8.3 rule 1's presentation requirement, resolvable by `import` with no artifact supplied.

title: a public generic works across modules even when its body reaches an internal helper
rule: Visibility inside a generic body is judged at the definition site: a public generic's body may reference its own module's `internal` declarations, and an external instantiation binds to them; the artifact interface must be sufficient for the consumer to type-check and instantiate the public generic with no access to `Helper`.

title: purity carries across the module boundary into a contract clause
rule: The artifact interface carries the purity modifier of every member it describes; a `requires` clause may call only `pure` members (§22.16), and that obligation is checkable against an imported member exactly as against a local one.

title: a default argument value crosses the artifact boundary
rule: The artifact interface must be sufficient for a consumer to type-check every well-formed use of the module's public surface, with full signatures — including default argument values.

title: a constraint violation at an external instantiation is diagnosed
rule: The artifact interface carries generic parameters with their variance and constraints; the consumer may instantiate a public generic only at type arguments satisfying them, so a type argument failing a declared constraint is diagnosed at the external instantiation.

title: a public generic instantiates at a consumer-declared type argument
rule: The artifact interface must be sufficient for a consumer to instantiate every public generic type at arbitrary module-external type arguments satisfying the declared constraints; an external instantiation behaves identically to a same-module instantiation at the same arguments.

title: a contract record carried in the interface is enforced at the consumer
rule: For every member the interface describes, it carries one contract record per contract clause — kind, `static` qualifier, canonical clause text, recorded tier; a `requires` clause runs in every build mode, so an imported member's precondition is enforced at the consumer's call site.

title: a type ascription naming a transitive type requires its own import
rule: Naming the type in source — in a type ascription, parameter or return type, `new` expression, cast, `is`/pattern type test, `catch` clause, explicit generic type argument, or extension declaration — requires importing its declaring module, even though `Money` reaches `App`'s compilation only transitively through `Lib1`.

title: importing a transitive type's own declaring module admits naming it
rule: Naming a transitively-reachable type in source requires importing its declaring module. Once `Base` is imported, `Money` may be named in a type ascription exactly as any other visible type.

title: use without import — an inferred binding needs no import of a transitive type
rule: A file that imports module `A` may freely use values of any public type reachable through `A`'s public surface — receive them into `using var` bindings with inferred types, call their public members, and dispose them — without importing the type's declaring module.

title: a new expression naming a transitive type requires its own import
rule: Naming the type in source — including in a `new` expression — requires importing its declaring module, even though `Money` is otherwise reachable through `Lib1`'s surface without one.

title: an is type test naming a transitive type requires its own import
rule: Naming the type in source — including a pattern/`is` type test — requires importing its declaring module.

title: an explicit generic type argument naming a transitive type requires its own import
rule: Naming the type in source — including an explicit (source-spelled) generic type argument — requires importing its declaring module.

title: the same type reached through two import paths is one type
rule: A type is identified program-wide by its declaring module name, qualified type name, and generic arity. `App` imports `Lib1` and `Lib2`, both of which import `Base`, and `App` imports neither `Base` nor presents it twice by hand — `Money` arrives via both `Lib1`'s and `Lib2`'s interfaces and is one type: a value `Payroll.Net` produces flows into `Invoices.Total`'s parameter with no conversion.

title: the dependency closure reaches an arbitrarily deep transitive chain
rule: A build must present the artifacts of the root compilation's direct imports and, transitively, of every module those artifacts' interfaces reference. `App` imports only `Outer`; `Money` is two hops further away (`Outer` -> `Mid` -> `Base`), and using it needs no import at any level.

title: a generic instantiation's static state is one copy across independently compiled artifacts
rule: A process contains exactly one copy of each module's code and, for each type — including each generic instantiation — exactly one static state and one runtime identity, regardless of link mode and regardless of how many compilations emitted code for the type.

title: a qualifying Main in a library compilation is an ordinary method
rule: A library build has no entry point; a qualifying `Main` in a library compilation is an ordinary method — it is declared, compiled, and callable like any other static method.

title: a non-generic type has one static state across three artifacts
rule: A process contains exactly one copy of each module's code and, for each type, exactly one static state and one runtime identity, regardless of link mode and regardless of how many compilations emitted code for the type.

title: an interface variable may hold a boxed record value
rule: An interface variable is a reference; its underlying value may be a class instance, a boxed record, a boxed enum, or a boxed primitive.

title: value-typed assignment copies an independent value
rule: A value type is copied on assignment; each variable holds an independent value.

title: reference-typed assignment aliases the same heap object
rule: A reference type is shared on assignment; multiple variables may refer to the same heap-allocated object.

title: a user type may not be named after a reserved primitive alias
rule: The PascalCase standard-library names of the primitive value types and String are reserved type names: a program may not declare a user type whose name is one of them.

title: a non-reserved type name compiles
rule: The PascalCase standard-library names of the primitive value types and String are reserved type names; any other name is unaffected.

title: an ordinary library type name such as Stream may be shadowed by a user type
rule: This does not reserve other standard-library type names — only the PascalCase aliases of the primitive value types and String; an ordinary library type such as Array or Stream may still be shadowed by a user type.

title: the keyword and PascalCase forms of a primitive name the same static members
rule: Static members of the standard library type are accessible through either form: int.Parse, int.MaxValue, double.IsNaN.

title: the ordering operators on bool operands are a compile error
rule: Ordering (<, <=, >, >=) on every primitive except bool — the ordering operators on bool operands are a compile error.

title: the ordering operators on int operands compile
rule: Ordering (<, <=, >, >=) on every primitive except bool.

title: bitwise operators on bool operands are a compile error
rule: Bitwise (&, |, ^, ~) ... Not valid on bool, char, or floating-point types. Boolean operations use and/or/not, which short-circuit and have boolean-only semantics.

title: bitwise operators on int operands compile
rule: Bitwise (&, |, ^, ~) on byte, sbyte, short, ushort, int, uint, long, ulong.

title: default(int) is defined as the zero value
rule: defaultable classifies types for which default(T) is defined: every non-nullable value type whose components are recursively defaultable — the primitives among them.

title: default of a non-nullable reference type is a compile error
rule: Not defaultable: non-nullable reference types.

title: default of the nullable form of a reference type is null
rule: defaultable classifies types for which default(T) is defined: every nullable type T?.

title: a constructor-only record is not defaultable
rule: constructor-only classifies records declaring a constructor carrying a contract clause; such a record is not defaultable.

title: a record with no contract clause on its constructor is defaultable
rule: a record all of whose declared fields are defaultable and which is not constructor-only is defaultable.

title: auto-hashable records get a synthesized structural equality operator
rule: auto-hashable classifies records and value-like choices for which =, GetHashCode, and ToString are synthesized.

title: bool renders as True or False
rule: bool has two values, true and false.

title: an if condition of a non-bool type is a compile error
rule: Conditions of if/elif and while, and a case/catch arm's when guard, require bool.

title: an if condition of type bool compiles
rule: Conditions of if/elif and while require bool.

title: byte.MaxValue is 255
rule: byte | 8, unsigned | 0 to 255.

title: an out-of-range unsuffixed integer literal in an untyped context is a compile error
rule: In an untyped context, an unsuffixed integer literal exceeding int's range is a compile error directing to a suffix.

title: the same literal at a declared long target is a target-typed integer constant
rule: an unsuffixed integer literal whose value exceeds int's range is admitted at a declared integer target whose range contains it, taking that target's type.

title: a suffixed literal exceeding its suffix's range is a compile error
rule: A suffixed integer literal whose value does not fit the suffix's type is a compile error.

title: the same value under the ulong suffix fits
rule: A suffixed integer literal whose value fits the suffix's type is admitted (5000000000U exceeds uint's range — write 5000000000UL).

title: the boundary carve-out admits int.MinValue's magnitude as unary minus's immediate operand
rule: The decimal literal of magnitude 2^31 (unsuffixed) is admitted only as the immediate operand of unary -, denoting int.MinValue.

title: the same magnitude without the immediate unary-minus position overflows int's range
rule: Anywhere else those magnitudes remain errors — the magnitude alone overflows before the - applies.

title: floating-point division by zero produces infinity rather than raising
rule: floating-point division by zero produces one of these [Infinity, -Infinity, NaN] rather than raising an exception.

title: zero divided by zero produces NaN
rule: floating-point division by zero produces one of Infinity, -Infinity, or NaN rather than raising an exception.

title: a floating-point literal exceeding the type's largest finite value is a compile error
rule: a literal whose magnitude exceeds its type's largest finite value (1e999, or 1e40f against float) is a compile error.

title: a floating-point literal within range compiles
rule: A floating-point literal denotes the nearest representable value of its type, provided its magnitude does not exceed the type's largest finite value.

title: NaN equals NaN under reflexive equality
rule: NaN = NaN is true.

title: negative zero equals positive zero
decimal division by zero raises DivideByZeroException
rule: Division by zero raises DivideByZeroException.

title: decimal arithmetic exactly represents finite decimal fractions
rule: High-precision decimal floating-point ... Exact representation of finite decimal fractions.

title: char values compare by code-point value
rule: Character values compare by code-point value: 'A' < 'B'.

title: a surrogate code point is not a valid char value
rule: Surrogate code points (U+D800 to U+DFFF) are not valid char values.

title: a non-surrogate char literal compiles
rule: A single Unicode scalar value, 32 bits wide; surrogate code points are not valid char values, other code points are.

title: string Length returns the number of code points
rule: s.Length returns the number of code points in s. O(1).

title: string indexing returns the char at a zero-indexed code-point position
rule: s[i] returns the char at code-point position i, zero-indexed. O(1).

title: out-of-range string indexing raises IndexOutOfRangeException
rule: s[i] ... Out-of-range raises IndexOutOfRangeException.

title: a closed range slice includes both endpoints
rule: s[r] ... a closed s[a..b] includes both ends.

title: a half-open range slice excludes the upper endpoint
rule: s[r] ... a half-open s[a..<b] excludes the upper.

title: an open-ended range slice extends to the end of the string
rule: s[r] ... the open-ended forms (s[..b], s[a..], s[..]) extend to the start or end of the string.

title: string ordering requires non-nullable operands
rule: Ordering requires non-nullable operands: an operand of static type string? is a compile error.

title: string ordering with non-nullable operands compiles
rule: Ordering requires non-nullable operands.

title: the + operator performs no implicit ToString conversion
rule: The compiler does not implicitly convert other types to string; use interpolation or .ToString().

title: interpolation is the correct way to embed a non-string value
rule: The compiler does not implicitly convert other types to string; use interpolation or .ToString().

title: a method with no declared return type has the unit-type result
rule: () is the type with exactly one value, also written (). It is the return type of methods declared without an explicit return type.

title: IntPtr is available without an explicit import
rule: IntPtr and UIntPtr are compiler intrinsics ... These types live in the auto-imported System module.

title: sbyte does not implicitly convert to byte (same-width signed/unsigned)
rule: The following are never implicit: between signed and unsigned types of the same or narrower width (e.g. int -> uint, uint -> int, short -> ushort).

title: sbyte implicitly converts to short (admitted widening)
rule: sbyte implicitly converts to short, int, long, float, double, decimal (the §5.1 implicit-conversion table). Twin of s5_1_0001: same source type, a target the table admits instead of one it excludes.

title: int does not implicitly convert to uint (same-width signed/unsigned)
rule: The following are never implicit: between signed and unsigned types of the same or narrower width (e.g. int -> uint, uint -> int, short -> ushort).

title: int implicitly converts to long (admitted widening)
rule: int implicitly converts to long, float, double, decimal (the §5.1 implicit-conversion table). Twin of s5_1_0003: same source type, a target the table admits instead of one it excludes.

title: ushort implicitly converts to int (unsigned widens to a strictly larger signed type)
rule: Widening from unsigned to a strictly larger signed type (e.g. byte -> short, ushort -> int) is permitted because no value is lost.

title: float implicitly converts to double
rule: float implicitly converts to double (the §5.1 implicit-conversion table).

title: double does not implicitly convert to float
rule: Implicit conversions occur only as listed in §5.1's table; double to float narrows and is not among the table's rows. Twin of s5_1_0006: same pair, direction reversed.

title: char implicitly converts to int
rule: char implicitly converts to int, uint, long, ulong, float, double, decimal (the §5.1 implicit-conversion table).

title: decimal does not implicitly convert from double
rule: The following are never implicit: between decimal and binary floats (float, double).

title: decimal converts from double only through an explicit conversion
rule: decimal and binary floats are never implicit (§5.1); decimal(x) for binary-float x yields the nearest representable decimal value under an explicit conversion (§5.2). Twin of s5_1_0009: the same pair, spelled through the admitted explicit form.

title: an enum does not implicitly convert to its underlying integer type
rule: The following are never implicit: between an enum and its underlying integer.

title: an integer does not implicitly convert to bool
rule: The following are never implicit: between integers and bool.

title: comparing an int to zero is the legal spelling the rejected int-to-bool conversion needs
rule: Between integers and bool, conversion is never implicit (§5.1); a comparison such as n <> 0 produces bool directly. Twin of s5_1_0012: same source, the comparison in place of the rejected conversion.

title: a compile-time-constant int narrows implicitly to byte when its value fits
rule: An expression of integer type that is a compile-time constant implicitly converts to any integer type whose range contains its value: var b: byte := 50; is exactly such a conversion.

title: a compile-time constant whose value does not fit the target's range is a compile error
rule: A constant whose value does not fit the target's range is a compile error at the conversion site — never a silent truncation. Twin of s5_1_0014: same target, a value outside byte's range.

title: constant narrowing crosses signedness when the constant's value fits the target's range
rule: The rule is value-based, not type-based: the source may be a compile-time constant of any integer type, and the target any integer type whose range contains the value, across signedness: const N: long := 8; var b: byte := N; is well-typed.

title: a run-time int value does not implicitly narrow to byte even when it would fit
rule: The [constant-narrowing] rule applies to constants only; a run-time int value still requires the explicit byte(x) narrowing of §5.2. Twin of s5_1_0014: the same target, a non-constant source.

title: a non-nullable value implicitly converts to its nullable form
rule: For any type T, T implicitly converts to T? — for a value type, the present-value wrapping.

title: a derived class reference implicitly converts to its base class
rule: Reference conversions are implicit: class to base class, transitively, up to Object.

title: a base class reference does not implicitly convert to a derived class
rule: Implicit conversions occur only as listed in §5.1; a downcast from a base to a derived class is not among the listed reference conversions. Twin of s5_1_0019: same pair, direction reversed.

title: a value type implicitly converts to Object by boxing
rule: Reference conversions are implicit: any type to Object — value types (primitives, records, enums, non-owning inline arrays, the unit type) by boxing.

title: a call applicable through two co-equal reference conversions is an ambiguous compile error
rule: For overload resolution, reference conversions rank co-equal with the other implicit conversions: given M(a: Animal) and M(o: Object), the call M(dog) is ambiguous — upcast explicitly.

title: explicit int-from-double conversion truncates toward zero
rule: var i: int := int(d); // truncates toward zero.

title: a checked integer narrowing that does not fit raises OverflowException
rule: Integer narrowing raises OverflowException if the value does not fit.

title: an explicit conversion from int to bool is rejected
rule: bool(n) remains an error in both the implicit and explicit forms — a numeric-to-bool reading is partial and truthiness-shaped; write the comparison (n <> 0) instead.

title: casting a negative int to uint raises OverflowException
rule: A conversion between a signed and unsigned integer type of the same width is a checked narrowing: it raises OverflowException when the value is not representable in the destination type — a negative value cast to an unsigned type.

title: narrowing a double beyond float's finite range yields Infinity and never raises
rule: float(d) for double d rounds to the nearest float; a magnitude beyond float's finite range yields +/-Infinity and never raises — floating-point narrowing follows floating-point arithmetic's own overflow behavior.

title: an explicit conversion from bool to an integer yields 1 and 0
rule: An explicit conversion from bool to any integer type is admitted: int(b) yields 0 for false and 1 for true (total, never fails).

title: an explicit conversion from bool to double is rejected
rule: A bool source likewise does not convert to float/double/decimal (no blessed numeric reading) or char (a code point, not a number).

title: casting an integer in the surrogate range to char raises OverflowException
rule: Casting an integer to char requires the integer to fall in U+0000–U+10FFFF excluding the surrogate range; otherwise OverflowException.

title: casting an integer in the code-point range to char yields that code point
rule: Casting an integer to char requires the integer to fall in U+0000–U+10FFFF excluding the surrogate range; var c: char := char(n); // n must be a valid code point.

title: converting an out-of-range binary float to decimal raises OverflowException
rule: decimal(x) for binary-float x yields the nearest representable decimal value; NaN, +/-Infinity, and magnitudes outside decimal's range raise OverflowException.

title: converting decimal to double never fails
rule: double(m) and float(m) for decimal m round to the nearest representable binary value and never fail (float's and double's finite ranges exceed decimal's).

title: a constant operand the conversion would reject is a compile error at the site
rule: Where the operand of an explicit conversion is a compile-time constant whose value would raise `OverflowException` under any rule of this section — integer narrowing, the same-width signedness change, the integer-to-`char` code-point range, and the floating-point and `decimal` conversions — the conversion is a **compile error at the conversion site**, never a deferred runtime fault: `uint(-1)` is rejected where it is written.

title: the constant-operand rejection holds in unreachable code
rule: A faulting constant operand is rejected **where it is written** — the posture §5.1's constant narrowing, §5.4's constant enum cast, §6.5's constant shift count and §17.14's constant evaluation all take, which reject a faulting constant whatever its reachability.

title: a constant operand that fits converts at compile time and is admitted
rule: The rule reads the **operand**: a compile-time constant whose value the conversion admits is not rejected, and the conversion keeps its ordinary semantics — the rejection reaches only a constant whose value would raise `OverflowException`.

title: a nullable-to-nullable cast maps a null operand to null
rule: A null operand yields null; var y: long? := long?(x); // nullable to nullable; null stays null.

title: casting a null nullable to its non-nullable form raises NullReferenceException
rule: var m: int := int(n); // raises NullReferenceException if n is null.

title: a nullable cast of a present value that does not fit raises OverflowException
rule: A present value v converts by T(v) under that conversion's own semantics, including its runtime checks (OverflowException on a non-fitting present value).

title: a nullable cast of a present value that fits converts by the underlying conversion
rule: A present value v converts by T(v) under that conversion's own semantics; the nullable cast form T?(x) is admitted exactly when the corresponding non-nullable conversion T(v) is admitted.

title: a nullable cast to an enum applies the declared-constant check to a present value
rule: A present value v converts by T(v) under that conversion's own semantics, including its runtime checks — for an enum target, §5.4's declared-constant check included.

title: a nullable cast whose non-nullable conversion is inadmissible is rejected
rule: For a target type T, the nullable cast form T?(x) is admitted exactly when the corresponding non-nullable conversion T(v) is admitted from the non-nullable form of x's type — and bool(n) remains an error in both the implicit and explicit forms (§5.2).

title: an in-range int converts to its enum constant
rule: An integer-to-enum cast E(n) is checked against the declared constants: it succeeds exactly when n equals the underlying value of some declared constant of E, and yields that value.

title: an integer-to-enum cast of a constant equal to no declared constant is a compile error
rule: When n is a compile-time constant equal to no declared constant, the cast is a compile error at the cast site — the same posture as §5.1's constant-narrowing range error.
check: compile error at the cast site

title: an int-to-enum cast of a non-constant undeclared value raises OverflowException
rule: When n is not a constant, a value equal to no declared constant raises OverflowException at runtime, the diagnostic naming the enum type and the value.

title: FromUnderlyingOrNull returns null where the checked cast would fault
rule: Boundary code for which an undeclared value is an expected input branches instead of catching: every enum carries a compiler-provided static member E.FromUnderlyingOrNull(value: U): E?, which returns null where the cast would fault.

title: under duplicate constant values the declared-value set is the set of distinct values
rule: Under duplicate constant values (§10.2), the declared-value set is the set of distinct values: E(1) where Legacy := 1, Current := 1 yields that one value.

title: a widening cast from a byte-backed enum to int cannot fail
rule: int(p) is well-typed on every enum: for byte-backed Priority it is int(byte(p)) and cannot fail — the cast I(e) converts e to U and then applies §5.2's integer conversion I(u), so a widening never fails.

title: narrowing a long-backed enum value to int raises OverflowException out of range
rule: For long-backed HttpStatus, int(s) is int(long(s)) and raises OverflowException when a NON-CONSTANT value is outside int's range; a declared-constant operand outside it is a compile error at the cast site (v0.301). A local variable read is not a constant expression (§17.14).

title: integer addition whose mathematical result does not fit the result type raises OverflowException
rule: Operators +, -, *, /, mod, unary -, ++, and -- on integer types are checked for overflow. An operation whose mathematical result is not representable in the result type raises OverflowException.

title: integer division truncates toward zero
rule: Division / between two integers truncates toward zero. var q := -7 / 3; // -2.

title: mod follows the dividend's sign
rule: mod follows the dividend's sign. var r := -7 mod 3; // -1.

title: integer division by zero raises DivideByZeroException
rule: Division and mod raise DivideByZeroException when the right operand is zero.

title: integer mod by zero raises DivideByZeroException
rule: Division and mod raise DivideByZeroException when the right operand is zero.

title: a compile-time constant that overflows is rejected, never deferred to runtime
rule: An evaluation fault — integer or decimal overflow, division or mod by zero, a shift count outside the §6.5 domain — is a compile error at the constant expression, never a deferred runtime fault: const B := 2147483647 + 1;.
check: compile error at the constant expression

title: mod is not defined on float or double
rule: mod is not defined on float or double; an expression of the form x mod y where either operand has a binary floating-point type is a compile error.

title: mixed int/long arithmetic promotes the int operand and the result has the wider type
rule: When operands have different types, the smaller-range operand is implicitly promoted to the larger type. The result has the larger type.

title: arithmetic between double and decimal has no implicit conversion and is a compile error
rule: If no implicit conversion exists between the operand types (e.g. double and decimal), the operation is a compile error and an explicit cast is required.

title: floating-point overflow produces Infinity rather than raising
rule: float and double arithmetic follows IEEE 754. Overflow produces +/-Infinity. No exception is raised.

title: 0.0 / 0.0 produces NaN
rule: Operations involving NaN propagate NaN. Division by zero produces +/-Infinity or NaN. No exception is raised.

title: a nonzero double divided by zero produces Infinity rather than raising
rule: Division by zero produces +/-Infinity or NaN. No exception is raised.

title: decimal arithmetic that overflows raises OverflowException
rule: decimal arithmetic raises OverflowException on overflow and DivideByZeroException on division by zero. There is no Infinity or NaN for decimal.

title: decimal division by zero raises DivideByZeroException
rule: decimal arithmetic raises OverflowException on overflow and DivideByZeroException on division by zero.

title: the bitwise AND operator is not valid on bool
rule: Operators &, |, ^, <<, >>, and unary ~ operate on the binary representation of integer values. They are not valid on bool, char, or floating-point types.

title: bitwise complement of a signed integer equals negation of the value plus one
rule: ~x is the bitwise complement; for signed types, ~x = -(x + 1).

title: bits shifted beyond the left operand's width are discarded silently and the result never faults
rule: Within the domain, bits shifted beyond the left operand's width are discarded silently — that is the operation, exactly as & discards bits — and the result never faults.

title: a compile-time-constant shift count outside the left operand's width domain is a compile error
rule: A count outside the domain — negative, or >= width — is a fault: a compile error when the count is a compile-time constant.

title: a non-constant shift count outside the domain raises OverflowException at runtime
rule: A count outside the domain ... raises OverflowException at runtime otherwise.

title: a compound assignment on a narrower integer target writes back through a checked narrowing
rule: When T is an integer type or char and R is an integer type, the result is converted back to T by the corresponding §5.2 checked narrowing: b += 10 on b: byte is b := byte(b + 10).

title: a compound assignment's narrow-integer write-back raises OverflowException out of range
rule: b += 10 on b: byte is b := byte(b + 10) — the addition runs in int per §6.2, and a result outside byte's range raises OverflowException — never a silent truncation.

title: a read-modify-write compound assignment on a nullable operand is a compile error
rule: A read-modify-write compound assignment is a compile error when the static type of its left-hand side, or of its right operand, is a nullable type — the desugared x op e has no meaning on a nullable operand.

title: ++ is not a user-overloadable operator token
rule: Unary operators have no compound forms; ++/-- are not overloadable (v0.289) — declare operator +, write c := c + 1;.

title: a compound assignment evaluates each constituent of its left-hand side exactly once
rule: Every constituent of the left-hand side's lvalue chain is evaluated exactly once, left to right — including every index expression in the chain.

title: a compound assignment evaluates chain, getter, right operand and setter in that order
rule: The order is: the LHS chain's constituent expressions, then the final segment's getter (where applicable), then e, then the operation, then the store; when the final segment is accessor-mediated, its getter and setter are each invoked exactly once.

title: the right operand of ??= is evaluated only when the assignment occurs
rule: ??= is not a read-modify-write: x ??= e assigns e only when x's current value is null. The LHS chain is evaluated once, the getter once; e is evaluated — and the setter invoked — only when the assignment actually occurs.

title: after ??= the target is narrowed non-null and admits the ordinary compound form
rule: ??= is unaffected — it is not a read-modify-write, and the absent case is its whole purpose; after x ??= e; the target is narrowed non-null (§7.4), so the ordinary compound form applies to it from the next statement on.

title: a double-typed result against a float target is a compile error
rule: In every other case the compound form is a compile error naming the explicit remedy — notably a binary-float or decimal result against a different LHS type (f += 2.5 where f: float promotes to double): write f := float(f + 2.5); when that loss is intended.

title: a float-typed result against a float target stores directly
rule: Let T be the left-hand side's type and R the type of x op e; if R is T, or R implicitly converts to T, the result is stored directly — write f += 2.5f; float promotion stays in-family.

title: a constant shift count outside the left operand's domain is rejected in <<=
rule: x <<= k and x >>= k inherit §6.5's count-domain rule through the desugaring: an out-of-domain count is the same fault — compile error for a constant count, OverflowException at runtime otherwise.

title: a non-constant shift count outside the domain raises OverflowException in <<=
rule: x <<= k and x >>= k inherit §6.5's count-domain rule through the desugaring: an out-of-domain count is the same fault — compile error for a constant count, OverflowException at runtime otherwise.

title: a nullable right operand to a read-modify-write compound assignment is rejected
rule: A read-modify-write compound assignment is a compile error when the static type of its left-hand side, or of its right operand, is a nullable type — either position, or both.

title: a nullable reference-typed target of += is rejected
rule: A read-modify-write compound assignment is a compile error when the static type of its left-hand side is a nullable type — a nullable reference-typed target included: the desugared x op e has no meaning on a nullable operand.

title: the narrow-integer write-back does not extend to a plain assignment
rule: The write-back is scoped to the compound form only: plain b := b + 10 remains the §6.2/§5.1 compile error it has always been, so the no-implicit-narrowing rule is undisturbed everywhere else.

title: a non-nullable reference implicitly converts to its nullable form
rule: A non-nullable reference type implicitly converts to its nullable form.

title: a nullable reference does not implicitly convert to its non-nullable form
rule: The reverse (nullable to non-nullable) requires a null check or `!`.

title: a nullable value type either holds a value or null
rule: A value type wrapped in `?` is an optional: it either holds a value or `null`.

title: assigning null to a non-nullable local is rejected
rule: Assigning `null` to a non-nullable target is a compile error.

title: assigning null to a nullable local is admitted
rule: Assigning `null` to a non-nullable target is a compile error (contrapositive: a nullable target admits it).

title: member access on an unnarrowed nullable value is rejected
rule: Member access, method calls, and indexing on a nullable value are compile errors unless the compiler has narrowed it to non-null.

title: a null test narrows the true branch for member access
rule: A null test — `x <> null` — narrows the true branch, admitting member access there.

title: an early exit on the null branch narrows the surviving path
rule: An early exit — after `if x = null then return; end;` — narrows the surviving path.

title: is not null narrows to the non-nullable form
rule: `x is not null` narrows to the non-nullable form.

title: a mutable field never narrows, even after a null check
rule: The compiler narrows local variables and `readonly` fields; it never narrows mutable fields or properties.

title: copying a mutable field to a local admits narrowing on the copy
rule: The standard pattern is to copy a nullable field to a local before narrowing; local-variable narrowing then applies to the copy.

title: reassignment from a nullable expression invalidates narrowing
rule: The narrowing of a variable is invalidated when, within the controlled block, the variable is reassigned from a nullable-typed expression.

title: passing a narrowed local as a ref argument invalidates narrowing
rule: The narrowing of a variable is invalidated when, within the controlled block, the variable is passed as a `ref` or `out` argument (the callee may reassign it).

title: a nullable readonly field narrows across an intervening call
rule: A nullable `readonly` field participates in flow narrowing, because outside its construction window it has no writer on any path, through any alias, so no call can invalidate a fact about its value.

title: a mutably-captured local loses its narrowing at an intervening call
rule: A variable that is mutably captured — assigned anywhere inside any lambda of the enclosing function body — loses its narrowing once the controlled block performs any operation that can transfer control to user code, such as a method call.

title: null-conditional access performs the access when the receiver is non-null
rule: `x?.M` returns null if `x` is null; otherwise it performs the access. The result type is always nullable.

title: a null receiver skips the whole chain, including argument expressions
rule: If a null receiver is found, nothing to the right of it in the chain is evaluated — no member is read, no call is performed, and the argument expressions of the skipped suffixes are not evaluated: `user?.Log(Render(x))` calls neither `Log` nor `Render` when `user` is null.

title: a null segment anywhere in a chain makes the whole chain null
rule: If any segment of a chain is null, the remainder of the chain is skipped on the same terms and the whole chain's result is `null`.

title: a null-conditional call on a null function value is a no-op
rule: A function value of nullable function type may be invoked with `?(...)`; the invocation is a no-op when the function value is null.

title: argument expressions of a null-conditional call are not evaluated when null
rule: When the function-valued operand is null, the invocation does not occur and the argument expressions are not evaluated — `handler?(Next())` does not call `Next` when `handler` is null.

title: null-coalescing yields a non-nullable result when the right operand is non-nullable
rule: `a ?? b` returns `a` if non-null, else `b`; the result type is `T` when the right operand is non-nullable.

title: the right operand of ?? runs only when the left operand is null
rule: The left operand is evaluated exactly once, and the right operand is evaluated only when the left operand's value is `null` — when the left is non-null the right operand expression does not run at all.

title: mixing an owned arm and a borrowed arm of ?? is rejected
rule: When the operands are owned, `??` is a two-branch expression whose result ownership follows the meet rule of an if/else join: an owned arm mixed with a borrowed arm is rejected.

title: owned ?? owned is owned and the chosen value is discharged once
rule: When the operands are owned (or owned-nullable), `owned ?? owned` is owned — the chosen value is discharged once.

title: ??= evaluates its right-hand side and assigns only when the left is null
rule: The compound form `??=` evaluates its right-hand side, and invokes the setter, only when the assignment occurs.

title: null-forgiving on a non-null value yields the non-nullable form
rule: `x!` asserts non-nullness. The result is the non-nullable form of the expression.

title: null-forgiving on a null value raises NullReferenceException at runtime
rule: If `x` is null at runtime, `NullReferenceException` is raised.

title: a non-nullable field with no initializer and no constructor assignment is rejected
rule: Every non-nullable field must be either assigned a value in every constructor before the constructor returns, or given a field initializer at its declaration.

title: a non-nullable field assigned in the constructor is admitted
rule: Every non-nullable field must be assigned a value in every constructor before the constructor returns, or given a field initializer at its declaration.

title: a field initializer at declaration satisfies definite assignment
rule: Every non-nullable field must be given a field initializer at its declaration, as an alternative to constructor assignment.

title: reading a non-defaultable local before it is assigned is rejected
rule: Definite-assignment analysis applies the same rule to locals, keyed on the same property: a local of **non-defaultable** type must be assigned before it is read. A non-nullable class type is the common non-defaultable case.

title: a non-defaultable local assigned before its read is admitted
rule: A local of non-defaultable type must be assigned before it is read; once assigned, a read is admitted.

title: a nullable local declared without an initializer holds null
rule: A local of defaultable type can be declared without an initializer — it gets the type's default, `null` for a nullable local.

title: a defaultable field with no initializer satisfies the rule vacuously
rule: A field whose type is defaultable satisfies the must-initialize rule vacuously and is implicitly initialized to that default; an explicit initializer is permitted and overrides it.

title: a field of an enum type with no zero-valued constant needs an initializer
rule: A field whose type is not defaultable requires an explicit initializer: a field initializer, or assignment in every constructor. The compiler emits a definite-assignment error if neither path supplies a value. An enum type with no declared constant of underlying value 0 is not defaultable.

title: an enum field with a zero-valued constant is implicitly initialized to it
rule: A field whose type is defaultable satisfies the must-initialize rule vacuously and is implicitly initialized to that default; for an enum the default is the value with underlying integer 0.

title: a bare unconstrained type-parameter field must be explicitly initialized
rule: A field or local of bare type `T` under an unconstrained parameter follows the non-nullable-reference rules (must-initialize, no vacuous `null` default), since `T` may be instantiated non-nullable.

title: a bare unconstrained type-parameter field initialized from a constructor parameter is admitted
rule: A field or local of bare type `T` under an unconstrained parameter follows the non-nullable-reference rules (must-initialize); assignment in the constructor satisfies it.

title: a nullable value type does not satisfy where T: value
rule: `where T: value` restricts T to non-nullable value types. A nullable value type (e.g. `int?`) does not satisfy the constraint.

title: a non-nullable value type satisfies where T: value
rule: `where T: value` restricts T to non-nullable value types — primitives included.

title: a nullable reference type does not satisfy where T: class
rule: `where T: class` restricts T to non-nullable reference types — classes, interfaces, `string`, function types.

title: a non-nullable reference type satisfies where T: class
rule: `where T: class` restricts T to non-nullable reference types — classes, interfaces, `string`, function types.

title: arithmetic + does not lift over a nullable operand
rule: No operator lifts to a nullable type. An operand whose static type is a nullable value type is a compile error at every arithmetic operator.

title: coalescing a nullable operand to a value admits the arithmetic operator
rule: No operator lifts to a nullable type; the remedy is `??`, `!`, or a narrowing check before the operator applies.

title: the relational operator < does not lift over a nullable operand
rule: No operator lifts to a nullable type; `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` are rejected over a nullable operand because an ordering comparison over an absent participant has no defensible result.

title: null-forgiving before a relational operator admits it
rule: The rule reads the operand's static type, so an operand asserted non-null with `!` is a non-nullable operand and the ordinary operator applies to it unchanged.

title: string ordering requires non-nullable operands
rule: `s < t` performs ordinal lexicographic comparison; ordering requires non-nullable operands — an operand of static type `string?` is a compile error.

title: narrowing a nullable string first admits ordering
rule: `s < t` requires non-nullable operands; narrowing an operand to non-null admits the ordering operator on it (narrow first, §7.4).

title: there is no three-valued logic — a bool? operand at and is rejected
rule: There are no `bool?` logical operators. `and`, `or`, `not` operate only on `bool`; a `bool?` operand is a compile error.

title: and operates on a non-nullable bool operand
rule: `and`, `or`, `not` operate on `bool`; a non-nullable `bool` operand is admitted.

title: a relational pattern over a nullable scrutinee is rejected
rule: A nullable scrutinee — value or reference — is a compile error at a relational pattern: ordering admits no absent participant, and pattern position performs no narrowing.

title: separating the null case first admits a relational pattern on the rest
rule: The absent case is separated first and the ordering interrogated on the bound value — `case n of null => …, var m: int when m > 70 => …, _ => … end`.

title: user code cannot redeclare Object
rule: `Object` is a compiler intrinsic; method bodies are provided by the runtime. User code cannot redeclare or replace `Object`.

title: a class named MyObject is an ordinary declaration
rule: `Object` is a compiler intrinsic; user code cannot redeclare or replace `Object`. A type with any other name is unaffected.

title: GetType on a class instance answers a module-qualified Type.FullName
rule: `v.GetType()` returns the `Type` value for the runtime type of `v`; `Type.FullName` renders a named type qualified by its declaring module path.

title: GetType cannot be overridden
rule: `GetType` is non-virtual; runtime type identity is fixed at allocation and cannot be overridden.

title: overriding Equals without GetHashCode is rejected
rule: A type that overrides `Equals` must also override `GetHashCode`. The compiler enforces this.

title: overriding Equals together with GetHashCode is admitted
rule: A type that overrides `Equals` must also override `GetHashCode`. Declaring both together is admitted.

title: the default Equals for a class is reference equality
rule: The compiler generates a default `Equals` appropriate to each type kind; for a class the default is reference equality.

title: null equals null under the null-safe equality wrapper
rule: `a = b` invokes `a.Equals(b)`, with a null-safe wrapper: `null = null` is `true`.

title: operator overloading of = is not permitted on classes
rule: Operator overloading of `=` and `<>` is not permitted on classes; classes customize equality by overriding `Equals`.

title: a class with no operator overload uses default Equals via =
rule: Operator overloading of `=` and `<>` is not permitted on classes; classes customize equality by overriding `Equals`.

title: = on a class invokes the overridden Equals
rule: For classes, `=` always invokes `Equals`.

title: the default ToString for a class renders the qualified type name
rule: The compiler-generated default `ToString` for classes returns the type's qualified name, the module-path-qualified rendering `Type.FullName` defines.

title: the default ToString for an enum renders the qualified type name, not the constant's name
rule: For enums, the compiler-generated default `ToString` returns the type's qualified name (the stdlib `FullName` rendering), not the constant's declared identifier. `NameOf` is the separate table that answers the constant's identifier (§10.4).

title: an enum that declares ToString to return NameOf renders the constant's name
rule: An enum may replace its default `ToString` by declaring a `ToString(): string` member; the replacement is used by every consumer, including interpolation. An enum whose rendering should be the constant's name declares `ToString` to return `E.NameOf(this)`.

title: a move-only owning inline array cannot be boxed
rule: Move-only value types — owning inline arrays (`[N owned]T` and `[N owned]T?`) — cannot be boxed. Boxing a value type copies the value into a heap wrapper, but move-only types forbid copying.

title: a non-owning inline array boxes per the general rule
rule: Non-owning inline arrays (`[N]T` and `[N]T?`) are ordinary value types and box per the general rule.

title: boxing a nullable value type yields a null reference or a boxed non-nullable
rule: When a nullable value type `T?` is boxed: if the value is `null`, the result is a null `Object` reference; if the value is non-null, the result is a boxed `T` — the nullable wrapper is stripped during boxing.

title: a boxed borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a field
rule: The compiler enforces: a boxed borrow-bearing record value may not be stored in a location that could outlive the source of any borrow the record contains. The boxed copy on the heap holds the same borrowed references as the source record; it does not extend their lifetimes.

title: a positional record generates a primary constructor and read-only properties
rule: For each positional record, the compiler generates a primary constructor whose parameters are the positional fields, in declaration order, and public read-only properties, one per positional field, with the same names.

title: the auto-generated positional properties read back the constructor arguments
rule: A record may declare positional fields in parentheses after its name; the compiler generates a primary constructor whose parameters are the positional fields and public read-only properties with the same names.

title: positional-record equality compares all positional fields
rule: Value equality (=, <>) is based on all positional fields (those marked equality skip excepted), generated only when every participating positional field is of an admissible component type.

title: positional-record ToString renders TypeName(Field1 colon value1, ...)
rule: ToString is formatted as "TypeName(Field1: value1, Field2: value2)".

title: comparing a positional record with an inadmissible field type is rejected at the call site
rule: A positional record with an inadmissible field declares fine, but comparing it is a compile error rather than silent reference equality.

title: comparing a positional record with an admissible field type is accepted
rule: Value equality is generated when every participating positional field is of an admissible component type; comparing such a record is unrestricted.

title: a body record with only auto-properties and a method is auto-hashable
rule: A body-only record receives auto-generated =, <>, GetHashCode, and ToString over its auto-properties when every instance member is an admissible auto-property, a method, a computed property, an eligible operator overload, or a constructor.

title: auto-generated body-record ToString lists auto-properties in declaration order
rule: The generated ToString produces "TypeName(Prop1: value1, Prop2: value2)" over the auto-properties in declaration order.

title: computed properties are excluded from auto-equality and auto-ToString
rule: Computed (expression-bodied) properties are not part of the equality comparison or the ToString output even when they are visible on the public surface; equality and the auto-formatted representation are always over storage, never over derived values.

title: primitive, enum, string, and nullable components are all admissible
rule: Admissible component types include a primitive type, an enum, or string, and T? where T is admissible, compared by the null-safe = of section 8.4.

title: another auto-hashable record is an admissible component type
rule: Admissible component types include another record that is itself auto-hashable, applied recursively.

title: a non-owning inline array of admissible element type is an admissible component
rule: Admissible component types include a non-owning inline array [N]T or [N]T? whose element type is admissible, compared element-by-element.

title: an auto-hashable value-like choice is an admissible component type
rule: Admissible component types include a value-like choice that is itself auto-hashable, per section 35.7, recursively applying this same list to every case's payload fields.

title: an explicit field declaration disqualifies auto-hashable and equality use is rejected
rule: A body record is not auto-hashable when it contains an explicit field declaration (storage that is not an auto-property), unless the field is marked equality skip; = on such a record without an explicit overload is a compile error.

title: equality skip on an explicit field rescues auto-hashable
rule: A storage component marked equality skip is removed from the auto-equality membership computation; a member whose type is inadmissible, including an explicit field declaration, does not disqualify the record when marked equality skip.

title: overriding Equals and GetHashCode disqualifies auto-hashable and equality use is rejected
rule: An override of Equals or GetHashCode means the author has taken over equality; the record is therefore not auto-hashable, and =/<> are a compile error unless the author also declares the operator =/<> overloads.

title: declaring the operator overloads beside an Equals or GetHashCode override restores equality use
rule: = and <> on a record outside the auto-hashable set are a compile error unless the author also declares the operator =/<> overloads, along with Equals(Object?), Equals(T), and GetHashCode overrides as needed.

title: a homogeneous equality overload disqualifies auto-hashable and an undeclared Equals use is rejected
rule: A homogeneous operator =/<> overload disqualifies the record from auto-hashable; calling someRecord.Equals(other) on a non-auto-hashable record without a user-defined declaration of that member — the `override` spelling or the plain one — is a compile error. The error fires per member: Money declares Equals(Money) and not Equals(Object?), and the Object?-argument call is the member it does not declare.

title: overriding Equals(Object?) beside a homogeneous equality overload makes the direct call legal
rule: The compile error on a non-auto-hashable record covers Equals(Object?), Equals(T), and GetHashCode; it fires per member and a user-defined declaration of that member — the `override` spelling or the plain one — removes it for that member.

title: a zero-auto-property body record compares equal always and renders TypeName()
rule: A body-only record with zero auto-properties is auto-hashable; the generated = returns true for every pair of values, and the generated ToString produces "TypeName()".

title: virtual is rejected on a record member
rule: A record member may not be declared virtual, abstract, or sealed override (v0.297); record members are always dispatched statically.

title: abstract is rejected on a record member
rule: A record member may not be declared virtual, abstract, or sealed override (v0.297); record members are always dispatched statically.

title: sealed override is rejected on a record member
rule: A record member may not be declared virtual, abstract, or sealed override (v0.297); bare sealed on any member is already section 12.4's error, and this rule adds sealed override.

title: override is admitted on ToString and replaces the compiler-generated rendering
rule: override is admitted only on Equals, GetHashCode, and ToString; an override here names the Object slot the member fills and implies no chain.

title: override is rejected on a record member other than Equals, GetHashCode, or ToString
rule: override is admitted only on Equals, GetHashCode, and ToString, and is rejected on every other record member, whatever its kind: method, property, or indexer.

title: equality skip on a static field is an inert-annotation compile error
rule: The equality skip clause is admitted on storage components only; on a static member it is a compile error, mirroring section 9.8's inert-annotation rule, because a static member never participates in equality.

title: a record may combine positional fields with a body that adds further members
rule: A record may have both positional fields and a body; the auto-generated members are present and the body adds further members.

title: a combined-form body may not repeat the auto-generated primary constructor's parameter list
rule: The body may not declare a constructor with the same parameter list as the auto-generated primary constructor.

title: a combined-form body may not declare a property with a positional field's auto-generated name
rule: The body may not declare a property with the same name as a positional field's auto-generated property.

title: a record declaring positional fields may not declare a constructor carrying a contract clause
rule: The body may not declare a constructor carrying a contract clause; the auto-generated primary constructor can carry none, so no record declaring positional fields is constructor-only.

title: a positional field marked equality skip is excluded from equality but still constructed and rendered
rule: A positional field may carry equality skip; the field is excluded from equality but present, constructed, and rendered, and a skipped field's inadmissible type does not disqualify the record.

title: body-form properties may be declared with any mutability
rule: In the body form, properties may be declared with any mutability. Mutable records are permitted but are inadvisable.

title: a bare store resolving to the receiver's own storage is rejected in a record method body
rule: this binds a borrow of the receiver value; a store that would land in the receiver's own storage is a compile error at the member body, including a bare X := e resolving to the receiver's storage.

title: a compound assignment to receiver storage is rejected through its desugaring
rule: The rule keys on where the store would land; a compound assignment or ++/-- classifies through its section 6.6/17.6 desugaring as a store landing in the receiver's own storage.

title: constructor bodies are not receiver positions
rule: Constructor bodies are not receiver positions; a record constructor initializes the value under construction, and Width := width; is section 9.2's own canonical body-record initialization form.

title: an external store through a named binding on a settable auto-property remains legal
rule: Settable properties keep their purpose: an external store through a named binding's lvalue chain, such as r.X := 5 on a settable auto-property, remains legal, the store landing in r's storage, announced by the assignment itself.

title: a store that hops through a class-typed member leaves the receiver and is legal
rule: A chain that hops through a class- or interface-typed member leaves the receiver: a record's reference-typed fields are borrows, so a store beyond such a hop lands in the borrowed heap object, not in the receiver, and is legal.

title: a this-rooted chain to receiver storage passed as an out argument is the same store by other syntax
rule: A this-rooted chain reaching the receiver's own storage passed as a ref/out argument is the same store by other syntax; an out argument may be a property with an accessible setter.

title: with produces a copy with named fields replaced
rule: A with expression produces a new record value with named fields replaced; the original record value is unchanged.

title: with applies to a freshly constructed record value
rule: new Point(1, 2) with(Y := 9) has a record-typed source and is an ordinary record with applied to the freshly-constructed value; the discriminator is the source expression's type kind, never the presence of new.

title: with over a class-typed source is rejected
rule: The source expression must be record-typed; a with expression whose source is class-typed is a compile error naming this rule, the retired object-initializer reading.

title: a with target must be accessible at the use site under its declared accessibility
rule: A with target must be accessible at the use site under the member's own declared accessibility; a private auto-property is a valid target only inside the declaring record.

title: a with target that is a private auto-property is legal from inside the declaring record
rule: A private auto-property is a valid with target inside the declaring record.

title: with does not re-invoke the constructor and so does not re-validate cross-field invariants
rule: with copies field values directly; it does not invoke the record's constructor. A constructor that validates cross-field invariants is not re-run during with.

title: with over a constructor-only record's source is rejected
rule: A with expression whose source expression's static type is a constructor-only record is a compile error at the with expression, naming the property and the source type.

title: a record may implement an interface and provide the matching member
rule: A record may implement any number of interfaces that declare no settable property or indexer member.

title: a record cannot derive from another record
rule: A record cannot derive from another record or from a class (other than the implicit Object root).

title: a record cannot implement an interface that declares a settable property
rule: A record may implement any number of interfaces that declare no settable property or indexer member; a conformance naming an interface with one is rejected at the declaration, since a value kind supplies no receiver-storing accessor.

title: a record may implement an interface whose members are all read-only or methods
rule: A record may implement any number of interfaces that declare no settable property or indexer member.

title: a record cannot declare an owned field
rule: Records cannot have destructors, owned fields, or implement IDisposable.

title: a record cannot declare a destructor
rule: Records cannot have destructors, owned fields, or implement IDisposable.

title: a plain reference-typed field in a record is a borrow, not an owned obligation
rule: Reference-typed fields in records are always borrows; the record does not own what they point to.

title: a record whose only reference-typed field is a string is not borrow-bearing
rule: A record whose only reference-typed fields are of declared runtime-managed types (string, function types) is not a borrow-bearing record; runtime-managed values have unbounded lifetime by construction, so no borrow-lifetime rules apply.

title: a borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a non-null static field
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a static field of any type, except when every reference-typed field of the value is null.

title: a borrow-bearing record may not be constructed from a temporary
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be constructed from a temporary bound to one of its borrow-carrying fields; a construction argument that is a fresh call result not bound to a named location has a lifetime that ends at the construction expression.

title: a borrow-bearing record may not be stored in an instance field of a class
rule: A borrow-bearing record value may not be stored in an instance field of a class; a class instance's lifetime is not bounded by any borrow source's scope, so the store is rejected statically.

title: a borrow-bearing record in the null-source form may be stored in a static field
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a static field of any type, except when every reference-typed field (and every reference-typed slot of every inline-array field) of the value is null — the null-source form.

title: borrow-carrying is transitive through another borrow-bearing record field
rule: A field is borrow-carrying when its type is another borrow-bearing record, or a borrow-bearing choice (transitivity); such a record is itself borrow-bearing and may not be stored in an instance field of a class.

title: a record of runtime-managed fields is not borrow-bearing under transitivity
rule: A record whose only reference-typed fields are of declared runtime-managed types (`string`, function types) is not a borrow-bearing record, so a record holding one is not borrow-carrying through the transitivity clause either, and no borrow-lifetime rule applies.

title: a borrow-bearing record carrying a borrow of a local may not be returned
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be returned from a method whose return-type rules cannot establish a sufficient lifetime for every borrow the record carries.

title: a null-source borrow-bearing record value carries no borrow and may be returned
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be returned from a method whose return-type rules cannot establish a sufficient lifetime for every borrow the record carries; a null-source value — every reference-typed field null — carries none.

title: the static null-source quantifier reaches every reference-typed field
rule: The quantifier is over reference-typed fields, not over borrow-carrying fields alone: a field whose declared type is reference-typed but not borrow-carrying — a `string`, a function type — must be null too. `record Tok(Src: Object?, Name: string)` initialized `new Tok(null, "missing")` is therefore rejected.

title: a value whose every reference-typed field is null satisfies the quantifier
rule: The quantifier is over reference-typed fields, not over borrow-carrying fields alone, so a null-source value holds no reference of any kind. At `Name: string?`, `new Tok(null, null)` is admitted as a static.

title: a record-carried borrow may not be copied into a longer-lived collection
rule: A borrow-bearing record value may be copied into a collection only when every carried borrow's source provably outlives the collection's own binding scope; a store into a collection whose binding's scope strictly encloses a carried source's scope is rejected at the store site.

title: a record-carried borrow whose source outlives the collection may be copied in
rule: A borrow-bearing record value may be copied into a collection when every carried borrow's source provably outlives the collection's own binding scope; the check is the same structural scope comparison as section 28.3's borrow rules.

title: a record with only admissible primitive and string components is serialization-eligible
rule: A record or enum is serialization-eligible when it satisfies the synthesis-eligibility rule; declaring the conformance is the opt-in, and the synthesis is automatic when eligible.

title: a record with a class-typed serialized component is not serialization-eligible
rule: A record's serialized components must be record-admissible; a record with a class-typed serialized component is not serialization-eligible, a compile error at the conformance declaration naming the field.

title: serialized skip on a class-typed component rescues serialization-eligibility
rule: serialized skip excludes the component from both directions entirely; a serialized skip component whose type is not defaultable is a compile error, so the remedy uses a nullable class-typed field. The explicit constructor still binds the skipped component: synthesized Deserialize step 2 matches the record's components — the serialized ones together with every `serialized skip` one, which binds its `default(T)`.

title: serialized optional on a non-defaultable enum component is rejected
rule: A serialized optional component whose type is not defaultable is a compile error at the conformance declaration; a missing field would have no value to supply.

title: a record component that declares neither serialization interface is not admissible
rule: A component type is admissible as a serialized component when it is another serialization-eligible record **that itself declares `ISerializable`/`IDeserializable`**: the synthesized members reach the nested value's own `Serialize`/`Deserialize`, which the conformance is the sole source of, so a record shaped eligibly that declares neither interface is not an admissible component and naming one is the conformance-declaration error.

title: the same record component declaring the conformance is admissible
