rule: Bare `throw` (either form) outside a catch arm body is a compile error. It is valid only inside a catch arm body.

title: a catch-all arm whose body is the unit value suppresses the exception
rule: To deliberately suppress all catchable exceptions in a block, use a bare-`Exception` arm whose body is the unit value `()`; the `()` body makes the suppression syntactically explicit.

title: a method that may throw needs no exception declaration
rule: Methods do not declare which exceptions they may raise. The compiler does not enforce that callers handle particular exception types. Any exception may propagate from any method call.

title: an exception propagates undeclared through several call frames
rule: Any exception may propagate from any method call; none of the intermediate methods in the chain need declare it.

title: an ArithmeticException arm catches an OverflowException
rule: The inheritance hierarchy is relevant for arm ordering: an arm pattern of `ArithmeticException` matches both `OverflowException` and `DivideByZeroException`.

title: an ArgumentException arm catches an ArgumentNullException
rule: The inheritance hierarchy is relevant for arm ordering: an arm pattern of `ArgumentException` matches `ArgumentNullException`.

title: ArgumentException.ParamName holds the supplied parameter name
rule: `ArgumentException` exposes `public readonly property ParamName: string?;` — the `(message, paramName)` constructor supplies it.

title: ArgumentException.ParamName is null when not supplied
rule: `public readonly property ParamName: string?;   // null when not supplied` — the `(message)`-only constructor leaves it null.

title: the (message, cause) constructor snapshots the cause into CauseChain
rule: The `(message, cause)` constructor borrows `cause` for the duration of the call and copies its type name, message, and stack-trace text into the new exception's `CauseChain`.

title: the cause instance is never retained after chaining
rule: The cause instance is never retained — consistent with §31.1's caught-exception-is-a-borrow rule, no ownership machinery is needed, and the full diagnostic chain survives independently of the cause instance.

title: no Exception constructor accepts a SupersededChain argument
rule: No constructor populates or accepts `SupersededChain` — the chain is runtime-populated exactly as `StackTrace` is, so no constructor's purity classification changes.

title: SupersededChain is empty on an exception that superseded nothing
rule: `SupersededChain` (v0.259 — empty when nothing superseded). It starts empty and shares the empty-array representation, so an exception that supersedes nothing allocates nothing.

title: throw with an operand may appear as the right operand of ??
rule: `throw` — with an operand, or the bare re-raise — may appear in any expression position, per §17.12's throw expression and its bottom type.

title: throw with an operand may appear as an if-expression branch
rule: `throw` — with an operand, or the bare re-raise — may appear in any expression position; the bottom type unifies with the other branch's type in an if-expression.

title: a well-formed extern block declaring several methods is admitted
rule: An `extern` block opens with `extern` followed by a string-literal library name, optionally a `convention` clause, and ends with `end;`; each entry inside is an ordinary method declaration -- visibility, name, parameters, return type -- followed by `;`, with no body and no per-method `end`.

title: an extern method entry omitting visibility defaults to internal
rule: `extern` declarations may be `public` or `internal`, following the rules for module-level declarations; omitting the keyword defaults to `internal`, the module-level default.

title: an empty extern block is a compile error
rule: Empty `extern` blocks are a compile error.

title: an extern method declared static is rejected
rule: They may not carry `static`, `virtual`, `override`, `abstract`, or `sealed`.

title: an extern block nested inside a class is rejected
rule: They are always module-level -- never members of classes.

title: an extern method is called unqualified from within its declaring module
rule: From within the same module, they are called by name without qualification.

title: a bare library name resolves per platform convention
rule: The library name is a bare identifier without extension. The runtime resolves it according to platform conventions.

title: a full path library name bypasses runtime resolution
rule: For libraries with non-conventional names, a full path may be used as the library name; this bypasses runtime resolution and loads the file directly.

title: the convention clause selects a non-default calling convention
rule: The default calling convention is the platform-standard C convention. For non-default conventions, the `convention` clause specifies which. `cdecl` and `stdcall` are universally accepted.

title: every integer type, float, double and bool are FFI-compatible parameter types
rule: Only the following types may appear in `extern` method signatures: All integer types and `float`, `double`. `bool` -- passed as a 1-byte value.

title: Ptr<T> is admitted as a parameter, a return type, and inside an FFI function type
rule: `Ptr<T>` -- a typed foreign address; admitted as a parameter, as a return type, and inside FFI function types, marshalling as the pointer it is.

title: CString is admitted as a parameter and an owned nullable return
rule: `CString` -- null-terminated UTF-8 byte sequence.

title: an inline array of an FFI-compatible scalar is admitted as an extern parameter by address
rule: Inline arrays `[N]T` where the element type is an FFI-compatible scalar ... Admitted as parameters only, by address.

title: the nullable boundary forms CString?, WString?, RawBytes? and a nullable function type are admitted
rule: Nullable boundary forms: `CString?`, `WString?`, `RawBytes?`, and nullable FFI function types are admitted as possibly-NULL pointers.

title: a Bezel string parameter type is rejected
rule: Not allowed: Bezel `string` (use `CString` or `WString`).

title: an enum parameter type is rejected
rule: Not allowed: ... enums (declare the underlying integer type and cast explicitly at the boundary).

title: Array<T> as a parameter type is rejected
rule: Not allowed: ... `Array<T>`, `OwningArray<T>` and the other collections.

title: a record that is not C-compatible is rejected as a parameter type
rule: Not allowed: ... records other than the §32.13 forms.

title: a nullable value type parameter is rejected
rule: Nullable value types are rejected: `int?`, `bool?`, `IntPtr?`, `Ptr<T>?`, and nullable record forms have no C representation.

title: a RawBytes extern return type is rejected
rule: A `RawBytes` extern return type is rejected (a C function returns one value, and the two-slot shape has no return convention).

title: an inline array extern return type is rejected
rule: `[N]T` as an extern return type is rejected (C functions do not return arrays; declare `Ptr<U>`, or a C-compatible record with an inline-array field, per the actual C signature).

title: an owning inline array is not admitted at an extern parameter
rule: Owning inline arrays and inline arrays of other element types are not admitted.

title: ref and out are admitted on FFI-compatible scalar extern parameters
rule: On extern parameters whose type is an FFI-compatible scalar ...: `ref p: T` -- C sees `T*`, receiving the address of the caller's storage. `out p: T` -- same address passing.

title: out owned is not admitted on an extern parameter
rule: Not admitted, with reasons: `out owned` (ownership transfer through an out-slot has no defined native contract).

title: an owned parameter is not admitted on an extern method
rule: Not admitted, with reasons: ... `owned` parameters (no native contract for consuming a Bezel-owned argument).

title: scoped is illegal on an extern parameter
rule: `scoped` function-typed parameters are illegal on `extern` declarations: neither the storage obligations nor the quiescence guarantee can be verified across the FFI boundary.

title: a temporary inline-array argument at an extern call site is rejected
rule: A temporary or otherwise non-assignable inline-array argument is a compile error.

title: a callback may not capture a binding passed out to the same extern call
rule: A callback argument of the same extern call may not capture a binding passed `out` to that call -- a compile error.

title: CString cannot be constructed directly with new
rule: `CString`, `WString`, and `RawBytes` are FFI-boundary types. They cannot be constructed or manipulated directly in ordinary Bezel code; the standard library provides explicit conversion functions.

title: a caller-owned string return is discharged with using var
rule: Native functions returning a buffer the caller must free declare their return type as `owned CString` (or `owned CString?` when the function may return NULL); ownership transfers to the Bezel side and `using var` discharges it.

title: a borrowed IntPtr return is read with string.FromCStringPointer
rule: For native functions returning a string pointer that the caller does not own ... the FFI declaration's return type is `IntPtr`, not `CString`. The Bezel side reads through the pointer with `string.FromCStringPointer(p: IntPtr): string`, which copies into a fresh Bezel `string` without taking ownership of the original buffer.

title: IntPtr.Zero supports the null test
rule: `IntPtr.Zero` -- the null pointer (integer 0). `=` and `<>` for null tests.

title: IntPtr converts explicitly to and from long
rule: Explicit conversions to and from `long` and `ulong` are also compiler intrinsics: `IntPtr(longValue)` and `long(ptr)` use the standard explicit-conversion syntax and are not declared as operator overloads on the record.

title: IntPtr declares no arithmetic operator
rule: `IntPtr` is a compiler-intrinsic value type. Its members are: `IntPtr.Zero`, `=` and `<>` for null tests, and explicit conversions to and from `long` and `ulong`. `IntPtr` is opaque; no arithmetic operator is among them, and §25.4 admits no user-declared conversion or operator on it.

title: a static method reference is admitted at a plain callback parameter
rule: At a plain (un-`env`-paired) function-typed parameter, the callback must be a static method reference or a non-capturing lambda: both lower to a bare C function pointer with no environment.

title: a non-capturing lambda is admitted at a plain callback parameter
rule: At a plain (un-`env`-paired) function-typed parameter, the callback must be a static method reference or a non-capturing lambda.

title: a bound instance-method reference is rejected at a plain callback parameter
rule: A bound instance-method reference (`obj.Method`) and a capturing lambda are rejected there -- each carries an environment (the receiver / the captures) that a bare function pointer cannot represent.

title: a capturing lambda is rejected at a plain callback parameter
rule: A bound instance-method reference (`obj.Method`) and a capturing lambda are rejected there -- each carries an environment (the receiver / the captures) that a bare function pointer cannot represent.

title: a bound instance-method reference is admitted at an env-paired callback parameter
rule: The pair makes the callback parameter capture-admitting: any function value -- including a capturing lambda and a bound instance-method reference `this.OnRow` -- may be passed there.

title: a capturing lambda is admitted at an env-paired callback parameter
rule: The pair makes the callback parameter capture-admitting: any function value -- including a capturing lambda ... -- may be passed there.

title: env pairing does not combine with variadic(N)
rule: `env` pairing does not combine with `variadic(N)`: a variadic call's trailing-slot ABI is caller-shaped per call, and no corpus case pairs the two.

title: Interop.LastErrno is read synchronously before the error message is built
rule: `Interop.LastErrno()` reads the calling thread's C `errno` directly. It is valid only when read before the next extern call or runtime operation on the thread.

title: the symbol alias clause binds a declaration to a different symbol name
rule: The alias clause `:= symbol "name"`, written after the return clause, binds the declaration to the named symbol instead.

title: several declarations of different shapes may bind one symbol
rule: Several declarations, of any mix of shapes, may bind one symbol.

title: variadic(N) with N equal to the declared arity is the sound fixed-arity binding
rule: `N` equal to the arity is legal and load-bearing ("call this variadic symbol with zero variadic arguments" -- the only sound minimum-arity binding of a variadic symbol).

title: variadic(N) with N less than the declared arity passes the trailing parameters variadically
rule: `variadic(N)` on the symbol clause declares: the named symbol is a C-variadic function whose fixed parameters are the first N declared parameters; the remaining declared parameters pass in the symbol's variadic slots.

title: a float in a variadic position is rejected in favor of double
rule: Declaring `float`, `bool`, `byte`, `sbyte`, `short`, or `ushort` in a variadic position is a compile error naming the type to write ("C promotes `float` variadic arguments to `double`; declare the parameter as `double`").

title: Ptr<T> members are usable over admitted pointee types
rule: `T` is drawn from the FFI-pointee set: integer types, `float`, `double`, `bool`, `IntPtr`, `UIntPtr`, and C-compatible records.

title: Ptr<Ptr<T>> is not admitted
rule: `Ptr<Ptr<U>>` is not admitted (v1 decline; `Ptr<IntPtr>` plus explicit `FromIntPtr` re-typing expresses every `T**` shape).

title: Ptr<T> instantiated at a class type is rejected
rule: The pointee gate (per-instantiation): `T` is drawn from the FFI-pointee set; a class type is not a member of it.

title: Ptr<T> is admitted at a C-compatible record pointee
rule: `T` is drawn from the FFI-pointee set: integer types, `float`, `double`, `bool`, `IntPtr`, `UIntPtr`, and C-compatible records.

title: a record of only FFI-compatible scalar fields is C-compatible and admitted by address
rule: A record is C-compatible iff every field's type is an FFI-compatible scalar ... Admission -- by address: as `ref`/`out` extern parameters.

title: a record with a string field is not C-compatible and rejected as a ref parameter
rule: Everything else disqualifies: `string`, `char`, `decimal`, nullable types, enums, class/interface/function-typed fields.

title: a single-field record over an integer scalar is admitted directly by value
rule: Typed handles: the single-field admission. A C-compatible record with exactly one field, of integer or pointer scalar type, is FFI-compatible directly -- parameter, return, `ref`/`out`, and callback positions -- marshalling exactly as its field.

title: a single-field record over a double is not admitted directly by value
rule: Float/double single-field records join Stage D; `bool` is excluded to avoid pinning an aggregate-normalization rule nothing needs.

title: a qualifying Main in a dependency artifact is inert
rule: A public static method Main declared on a class in the root compilation is the entry point. A qualifying signature in a dependency artifact is inert — never selected, never a conflict, an ordinary method. `Dep` even declares two qualifying overloads, which would be a §33.5 ambiguity error in a root compilation, yet it compiles as a dependency and never perturbs `App`'s build.

title: a dependency's Main stays inert even when its class is used by the root
rule: Every Bezel executable has exactly one entry point: a `public static method Main` declared on a class in the root compilation. A qualifying signature in a dependency artifact is inert — never selected, never a conflict, an ordinary method — and that holds for a dependency class the root compilation actually references, not only for one it merely imports.

title: Main() with no parameters and no return type qualifies
rule: `public static method Main()` is one of the eight accepted entry-point signatures.

title: Main(args) with no return type qualifies
rule: `public static method Main(args: Array<string>)` is one of the eight accepted entry-point signatures.

title: Main(): int qualifies
rule: `public static method Main(): int` is one of the eight accepted entry-point signatures.

title: Main(args): int qualifies
rule: `public static method Main(args: Array<string>): int` is one of the eight accepted entry-point signatures.

title: async Main(): Task qualifies
rule: `public static async method Main(): Task` is one of the eight accepted entry-point signatures.

title: async Main(args): Task qualifies
rule: `public static async method Main(args: Array<string>): Task` is one of the eight accepted entry-point signatures.

title: async Main(): Task<int> qualifies
rule: `public static async method Main(): Task<int>` is one of the eight accepted entry-point signatures.

title: async Main(args): Task<int> qualifies
rule: `public static async method Main(args: Array<string>): Task<int>` is one of the eight accepted entry-point signatures.

title: a private static Main overload does not conflict with a qualifying one
rule: `Main` must be `public` and `static`. A signature outside the eight accepted forms does not qualify as an entry point; a method named `Main` with a non-qualifying signature is an ordinary method.

title: an instance Main overload does not conflict with a qualifying one
rule: An instance method named `Main` does not qualify. (A class may still declare a non-qualifying `Main` alongside a qualifying one.)

title: a class declaring two qualifying Main overloads is rejected
rule: A program is ill-formed if more than one method qualifies as the entry point ... within a single class (one class declaring more than one of the eight signature shapes). A class that overloads `Main` with multiple qualifying signatures is rejected at compile time.

title: only one overload qualifying resolves the entry point cleanly
rule: A class may declare at most one qualifying `Main`; making the second overload non-qualifying (here, `private`) removes the conflict.

title: two classes each declaring a qualifying Main is rejected
rule: A program is ill-formed if more than one method qualifies as the entry point. This applies across classes (multiple classes each declaring a qualifying `Main`). Without disambiguation, the compiler produces an error listing every qualifying `Main` it found.

title: only one class declaring a qualifying Main resolves cleanly
rule: An instance method named `Main` does not qualify; making the second class's `Main` an instance method removes the cross-class conflict.

title: standard documentation tags on a type and its members are accepted
rule: Documentation comments use XML element syntax. Recognized tags include `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>`; the compiler preserves them in output metadata for documentation generators.

title: an unrecognized documentation tag is preserved, not rejected
rule: Unrecognized tags are preserved verbatim in the same metadata: recognition affects only how documentation tooling may render a tag, never compilation.

title: a documentation comment not immediately before a declaration still compiles
rule: Documentation comments are meaningful only immediately before a declaration; the compiler preserves comments but does not interpret their content or restrict their placement.

title: a documented entry point compiles and runs unaffected
rule: The compiler preserves documentation comments for documentation generators but does not interpret their content — compilation and runtime behavior are unaffected.

title: a choice type satisfies the value constraint
rule: `where T: value` substitutions are non-nullable value types: records, enums, choices, primitives, inline arrays, the unit type.

title: a nullable choice type does not satisfy the value constraint
rule: `where T: value` substitutions are non-nullable value types — records, enums, choices, primitives, inline arrays, the unit type. A nullable value type does not satisfy the constraint.

title: a choice declares payload-free, value-payload, and owned-payload cases together
rule: A choice declares zero or more positional payload fields per case; a case with no payload list is payload-free; the owned marker is admissible on a class-typed payload field.

title: a case name colliding with a member name is rejected
rule: Case names must be distinct within the choice; a case name may not collide with any member name of the choice (the §11.3 member rules apply with cases counted as members).

title: duplicate case names within one choice are rejected
rule: Case names are PascalCase by convention and must be distinct within the choice.

title: a payload field of the choice's own type is rejected
rule: A choice payload field may not, directly or transitively through value-typed components, have the declaring choice's own type: a value type cannot contain itself.

title: a payload transitively containing the choice's own type via a record is rejected
rule: A choice payload field may not, directly or transitively through value-typed components (record fields, inline-array elements, other choices' payloads), have the declaring choice's own type.

title: owned on a primitive-typed payload field is rejected
rule: The owned payload marker's admissibility follows §28.1's type requirement: admissible on class types, interface types, and bare type parameters; a compile error on any other type.

title: owned on a move-only-value payload field is admitted but redundant
rule: The owned payload marker is admitted-but-redundant on move-only value types (an owning inline array, or another owning choice).

title: a destructor in a choice body is rejected
rule: Choices cannot have destructors, constructors, instance fields, block-form or storage-backed properties, indexers, or nested types — the same restriction set as enums, plus one: a choice's instance storage is its cases' payloads.

title: a constructor in a choice body is rejected
rule: Choices cannot have destructors, constructors, instance fields, block-form or storage-backed properties, indexers, or nested types.

title: an instance field in a choice body is rejected
rule: Choices cannot have destructors, constructors, instance fields, block-form or storage-backed properties, indexers, or nested types.

title: a choice body admits exactly what an enum body admits
rule: A choice body may declare, after the case list, exactly what an enum body may: instance methods, expression-bodied read-only instance properties, static methods, static readonly fields, const members, and operator overloads.

title: a virtual method on a choice is rejected
rule: Choice members are statically dispatched; virtual and abstract are rejected as on enums and records.

title: override on a non-Object-virtual choice member is rejected
rule: override is admitted exactly where §10.5 admits it — the Object-virtual surface, spelled override or plain — and is rejected on every other member.

title: override ToString is admitted on a choice
rule: §10.5's Equals/GetHashCode/ToString replacement rule carries over for the boxable classifications, spelled override or plain.

title: a plain Equals/GetHashCode member is declarable on an owning choice
rule: A choice of any classification — owning and borrow-bearing included — may declare plain Equals(other: C): bool and GetHashCode(): int members, statically dispatched like every choice method; on a non-boxable classification they replace nothing and are reachable by static dispatch only.

title: a Result combinator is rejected at an owning receiver instantiation
rule: Map, MapError, AndThen, and UnwrapOr are admissible only where the receiver instantiation and the member's result instantiation are both value-like (§35.4 rule 3); the rejection lands at the use site under §3.6 rule 2, the diagnostic naming the classification.

title: a static owned readonly field is admitted in a choice body
rule: A choice body may declare static readonly fields, including static owned readonly.

title: a declared homogeneous `=` overload on a choice replaces the generated one
rule: A choice body may declare operator overloads; records, enums, and choices may overload = and <>, and a homogeneous overload disqualifies the choice from auto-hashable, §25.2's co-declaration rule then supplying the equality surface.

title: qualified case construction resolves a payload-free and a payload case
rule: Construction is qualified, resolving exactly as enum constants do: FetchOutcome.NotModified for a payload-free case (a value expression, not a call), FetchOutcome.Failed(504, "upstream timeout") for a payload case.

title: a bare unqualified case name outside a declared-result position is rejected
rule: In expression position outside a declared-result position the qualified form is required, exactly as for enum constants outside their scrutinee.

title: a bare case construction in a declared-result position resolves against the declared type
rule: In a declared-result position — the top-level operand of a return statement in a body with a declared return type — where the declared type is a choice instantiation that declares a case named N, the form N(args) is a case construction.

title: generic choice construction omitting type arguments is rejected
rule: For a generic choice the type arguments are written at the construction; the declared type supplies the choice type and all its type arguments whole — the generic type with no arguments (Result.Ok(v)) remains an error.

title: generic choice construction with explicit type arguments is admitted
rule: For a generic choice the type arguments are written at the construction: Result<int, string>.Ok(value).

title: the declared-result case reading does not extend into a subexpression position
rule: The case reading takes exactly the declared-result group and does not extend beyond it — not to subexpression positions within a return operand: in return (if c then Ok(v) else Error(e)); the branches are operands of the (if) atom and resolve ordinarily.

title: a named owned binding to an owned payload slot requires the move marker
rule: An argument to an owned payload slot is an owned-consuming position: a named owned binding requires the call-site marker (move resp) and is left moved-from.

title: constructing a holds-borrows choice from a temporary is rejected
rule: An argument to a plain class- or interface-typed payload slot is a borrow, and §9.7's no-temporary-source rule applies verbatim: constructing a choice that holds borrows from a temporary bound to a borrow-carrying payload is rejected.

title: a value-like choice is an ordinary copyable value
rule: A value-like choice is an ordinary copyable value type: every payload is a value, a string, a runtime-managed type, or (transitively) a value-like record or choice.

title: owning choice local-to-local assignment moves, unmarked, and `using var` adopts
rule: Owning choices are move-only value types: local-to-local assignment moves (unmarked — copies are impossible, so there is nothing for a marker to disambiguate); `using var` is admitted with pin-only effect.

title: an owning choice that holds borrows may not be a class field
rule: An owning choice that holds borrows may not be a class field: it is the only move-only kind that can hold borrows, and the store would let the borrows outlive their sources.

title: disposing an owning choice disposes the active case's owned payloads in declaration order
rule: Disposal is defined by the active case. Disposing an owning choice value disposes the active case's owned payloads in payload declaration order; payload-free and value-payload cases dispose nothing.

title: drop-on-overwrite disposes the displaced owning-choice value at the store
rule: Drop-on-overwrite is defined and automatic: whole-value reassignment of an owning-choice local or field disposes the displaced value per §28.7; the RHS is evaluated first, then the displaced value is disposed, then the new value is stored.

title: Task<T> declared over an owning choice is a compile error at the declaration
rule: No §30.5 producer row admits a move-only value result, so a Task<T> or OwningTask<T> declared over an owning choice is a compile error at the declaration.

title: an owning-choice local under plain var auto-disposes at scope end and warns
rule: Owning choices are move-only value types; locals are auto-disposed at scope end with the must-use warning (K3.14). Disposal is defined by the active case: it disposes the active case's owned payloads.

title: using var over an owning choice suppresses the must-use warning
rule: `using var` is admitted over an owning choice — it locks reassignment and suppresses the must-use warning on that auto-drop, the auto-dispose running either way.

title: an owning choice may not be a record field
rule: Owning choices are move-only value types and every section 15.3 rule applies as written: no move-only value may be a record field (records support only copy semantics, not move semantics).

title: a value-like choice is copyable and may be a record field
rule: Otherwise the choice is value-like: every payload is a value, a `string`, a runtime-managed type, or transitively a value-like record or choice. A value-like choice is an ordinary copyable value type, so section 15.3's move-only record-field ban does not reach it.

title: a choice that holds borrows is forbidden as an async parameter
rule: Every choice that holds borrows — whatever its classification — is subject to section 9.7's borrow-lifetime rules, and is forbidden as an `async` method's parameter or result (section 30.1).

title: a value-like choice holds no borrows and is admitted as an async parameter
rule: A value-like choice never holds borrows (rule 3's construction), so section 30.1's ban on a borrow-bearing parameter of an `async` method does not reach it.

title: the borrowing match is the default and leaves the scrutinee unchanged
rule: Matching a choice value non-destructively is the default everywhere: a pattern binding is a borrow whose source is the scrutinee's source; the scrutinee retains its ownership state; the construct never moves from the scrutinee.

title: an owning match is triggered by an unbound owned temporary
rule: The owning match is triggered by an unbound owned temporary of owning-choice classification — a fresh construction, an owning-choice-returning call, a move result; it transfers the selected case's owned payloads into the arm's bindings and consumes the scrutinee value.

title: an owning match is triggered by a named owned binding under `case move`
rule: The owning match is triggered by a named owned binding under an explicit scrutinee transfer marker — case move outcome of ...; the consumed binding is left moved-from when the construct completes.

title: the move marker on a fresh-producer scrutinee is rejected
rule: The marker on a borrowed or fresh-producer scrutinee is an error: an unmarked read never silently consumes, and a fresh producer needs no marker.

title: the move marker on a borrowed scrutinee (`this`) is rejected
rule: What does not trigger an owning match: an unmarked named-binding scrutinee; a borrowed scrutinee of any provenance (field read, parameter, this).

title: a discarded owned payload is disposed at construct completion
rule: Payloads not transferred into bindings — discarded slots like Fetched(_) — are disposed when the construct completes, by the same unbound-temporary pass that disposes the container.

title: a payload case matched bare with no arity is rejected
rule: A payload case may not be matched bare: Fetched without parentheses is a compile error naming the arity — matching a payload while ignoring it is spelled visibly as Fetched(_).

title: a marked named slot transfers its payload at arm selection
rule: A named slot may carry the transfer marker on its source: Fetched(move response = var r) transfers the payload into r at arm selection, exactly as the corresponding positional slot would.

title: a marked named slot in a borrowing match is rejected
rule: The marker on a slot of a borrowing match is a compile error: the scrutinee retains ownership, so no slot can mint an obligation from it.

title: an unmarked named slot does not transfer, so its binding cannot be moved
rule: An unmarked named slot never transfers: in an owning match an owned payload matched by an unmarked named slot is borrowed during the arm and disposed at construct completion, exactly as a discarded slot.

title: an owning-match arm binding left owning auto-drops with the must-use warning
rule: In an owning match, an `owned`-payload binding is an **owned local of the arm body's scope** ...: falling off the arm still owning the value auto-drops it with the must-use warning naming the binding and the standard remedies.

title: the using var move adoption in a do-end arm is warning-free
rule: The standard remedies are `using var u := move r;` adoption in a `do … end` arm, an owned-consuming call, an explicit `r.Dispose()`, `_ := r;`.

title: an owned-consuming call is an expression-position arm's warning-free discharge
rule: In *expression-position* arms (which cannot contain statements, §19.2), the warning-free discharges are an owned-consuming call (`RenderOwned(move r)`) or §19.2's helper-method extraction.

title: every declared case covered by an irrefutable arm needs no `_` arm
rule: Coverage is counted per case name, one level deep — a payload-free case by a constant-style pattern, a payload case by a destructuring whose every slot is irrefutable. When every case is covered, no _ arm is required.

title: a refutable slot arm contributes nothing to exhaustiveness
rule: Guarded arms and refutable-slot arms contribute nothing to the static proof for choice scrutinees.

title: a value-like choice is auto-hashable and its `=` compares active case and payloads
rule: A value-like choice is auto-hashable when every payload field of every case is an admissible component type. The generated = is true exactly when both operands have the same active case and every corresponding payload compares equal by its type's =.

title: the generated ToString renders TypeName.CaseName with its payloads
rule: The generated ToString produces TypeName.CaseName(field1: value1, ...), and TypeName.CaseName for a payload-free case.

title: comparing a non-auto-hashable owning choice without declared operators is a use-site error
rule: A choice that is not auto-hashable — any borrow-bearing or owning choice — draws a use-site compile error on =, <>, and direct Equals/GetHashCode calls, unless the author declares the operators under §25.2's co-declaration rule.

title: co-declared equality operators on a move-only choice bind borrows
rule: On a move-only choice, = / <> operands and the Equals(T) parameter bind borrows — both operands stay live after the operation.

title: direct Equals and GetHashCode calls are admitted on an owning choice that declares them
rule: The exemption for **direct `Equals`/`GetHashCode` calls** is keyed on the declared **members**, not on the operators: a choice that declares plain `Equals(other: C): bool` or `GetHashCode(): int` admits THAT call on **every** classification, owning and borrow-bearing included — they resolve statically to the declared members, so the exemption is per member and needs no pair (v0.301).

title: a direct Equals call on an owning choice that declares no such member is rejected
rule: A choice that is **not** auto-hashable — any borrow-bearing or owning choice — draws §9.2's use-site compile error on `=`, `<>`, and direct `Equals`/`GetHashCode` calls, unless the author declares the member itself.

title: a value-like choice boxes through interface conformance
rule: Value-like choices box per the general rule; the box is runtime-managed.

title: converting an owning choice to an interface is a rejected boxing conversion
rule: Owning choices cannot be boxed. The conformance declaration remains legal, but the conversion of an owning value to an interface or Object type is rejected at the conversion site.

title: calling Dispose on a choice value is rejected
rule: Dispose stays off the surface everywhere: choices do not implement IDisposable — an owning choice's disposal obligation is discharged by its holder, never by calling Dispose() on it.

title: assigning null into an owned-state C? location disposes the displaced value
rule: For an owning C, x := null; on an owned C? location is drop-on-overwrite — the displaced value's payloads are disposed.

title: default(C?) is a valid null move-only value for an owning C
rule: For an owning C, the wrapper C? is itself move-only, and default(C?) is a valid null move-only value, on the precedent of §17.11's owning-inline-array form.

title: default(C) is a compile error for every choice type
rule: default(C) is a compile error for every choice type — no choice is defaultable: a sum yields no distinguished zero.

title: choices never satisfy where T: new()
rule: Choices never satisfy the value-type arm of where T: new() — a consequence of the property: no choice is defaultable.

title: nameof on a choice case yields the case's bare identifier
rule: nameof(FetchOutcome.Failed) yields "Failed".

title: a generic choice's classification is evaluated per instantiation
rule: Classification is evaluated per instantiation: a choice with Ok(owned value: T) is value-like at T = int (marker erased, payload an admissible value) and owning at T = Connection (marker means owned).

title: choices are invariant in their type parameters
rule: No variance. Variance attaches to interface and function-type parameters only; choices, like records and classes, are invariant. A Result<Derived, E> is not a Result<Base, E>; the conversion is an explicit re-wrap by match.

title: a borrow-bearing choice is never sendable
rule: Borrow-bearing choices are never sendable (they carry origin-domain borrows).

title: an owning choice is not directly sendable
rule: Owning choices are not directly sendable — the §30.14 move-only exclusion, unchanged.

title: an owning-choice field of a transfer-closed class is admitted when the choice holds no borrows
rule: §30.14's transfer-closure rule 2 admits an owning-choice-typed field of a transfer-closed class when the choice holds no borrows and every payload field of every case is transfer-compatible.

title: a choice type in an extern signature is rejected
rule: Choices are not FFI-compatible: the honest C spelling of a sum carries real ABI questions the language does not promise to resolve.

title: ReadKey is the assert-shaped throwing tier at end of input
rule: Console.ReadKey() blocks for one key and raises EndOfStreamException at end of input; per the failure-signal rule, end of input is band 2's expected absence, but ReadKey stays the throwing tier because absence there is a bug at its call sites.

title: ReadKeyOrNull is the *OrNull twin, answering the same absence with null
rule: The *OrNull convenience tier answers the same expected-absence condition its throwing twin raises on; Console.ReadKeyOrNull() returns null at end of input where Console.ReadKey() raises EndOfStreamException.

title: a negative constructor magnitude raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException
rule: Every constructor parameter that states a magnitude -- capacity, size, length -- raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException when passed a negative value; StringBuilder(capacity) is one of the named members.

title: a zero constructor magnitude is valid, not a fault
rule: Negative magnitudes fault; zero is valid -- a magnitude-taking constructor such as StringBuilder(capacity) constructs successfully at capacity zero, and the instance is fully usable afterward.

title: Try shape (c) assigns default(T) to the out parameter on the false path
rule: Try shape (c) -- bool + non-nullable value-typed out -- assigns default(T) to the out parameter when the operation declines. Convert.TryToInt32 is this shape over a concrete value-type payload.

title: Try shape (c) assigns the parsed value on the true path
rule: Try shape (c) assigns the real, non-default value to the out parameter when the operation succeeds; Convert.TryToInt32 returns true and the parsed integer on well-formed input.

title: ReadLine returns null at end of input
rule: Console.ReadLine() returns null at end of input.

title: WriteLine(Object) invokes the argument's ToString override
rule: The Object overloads of Console.Write/WriteLine invoke ToString().

title: Write does not append a line terminator, unlike WriteLine
rule: Console.Write(value) writes value with no terminator; consecutive Write calls land on the same output line, unlike WriteLine which terminates it.

title: Out exposes the process's standard-output stream
rule: Console is a static class providing process-level standard output, and Out is a readonly TextWriter property over it; a file that imports a module may call the public members of a value reachable through its surface without importing the value's own declaring module (System.IO).

title: Round uses banker's rounding at a midpoint
rule: Math.Round(x, digits) rounds using banker's rounding; a midpoint such as 2.5 rounds to the nearest even integer, 2, not 3.

title: Clamp raises ArgumentException when low exceeds high
rule: Math.Clamp<T>(value, low, high) raises ArgumentException when low is greater than high.

title: DivRem raises DivideByZeroException when the divisor is zero
rule: Math.DivRem(a, b, out remainder) raises DivideByZeroException when b = 0, the same fault the / operator raises.

title: Sign yields 0 for NaN rather than -1 or 1
rule: Math.Sign<T>(x) is two < tests against T.Zero(), so a NaN operand yields 0.

title: Fmod and IEEERemainder may disagree in sign on the same operands
rule: Fmod(x, y) returns a result with the same sign as x; IEEERemainder(x, y) may have the opposite sign from x -- unlike Fmod.

title: ToInt32 raises FormatException on a non-numeric string
rule: Convert.ToInt32(value) raises FormatException when the string is not a well-formed representation of the target type.

title: ToInt32 raises OverflowException when the value does not fit
rule: Convert.ToInt32(value) raises OverflowException when the value does not fit the target type.

title: ToString(value, toBase) rejects a base outside {2, 8, 10, 16}
rule: Convert.ToString(value, toBase) accepts only bases 2, 8, 10, and 16, raising ArgumentException otherwise.

title: ToBoolean accepts "true"/"false" case-insensitively
rule: Convert.ToBoolean(value) accepts exactly "true"/"false", case-insensitively -- Boolean.Parse's contract.

title: Get returns null when the variable is absent
rule: Environment.Get(name) returns null when the variable is absent.

title: Set(name, null) removes the variable
rule: Environment.Set(name, value) with value = null removes the variable.

title: Set raises ArgumentException for an empty variable name
rule: Environment.Set(name, value) raises ArgumentException when name is empty, or contains "=".

title: GetInt conflates a malformed value with an absent one, returning null
rule: Environment.GetInt(name) returns null when the variable is absent OR malformed -- deliberately conflated.

title: DateTime's no-format ToString renders ISO 8601
rule: The no-argument DateTime.ToString() renders the round-trippable ISO 8601 form yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.

title: an invalid DateTime component raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException
rule: The DateTime constructors raise ArgumentOutOfRangeException on invalid components, such as a month outside 1..12.

title: Parse accepts the date-only form with zero time components
rule: DateTime.Parse accepts the date-only form yyyy-MM-dd, with time components zero.

title: Parse raises FormatException on a non-conforming string
rule: DateTime.Parse accepts exactly the round-trip form, its fractional- seconds extension, and the date-only form; any other input raises FormatException.

title: ParseOrNull returns null exactly where Parse raises
rule: DateTime.ParseOrNull(s) returns null exactly where Parse(s) raises; otherwise the parsed value.

title: TimeSpan subtraction computes the elapsed duration
rule: TimeSpan declares operator -(a, b): TimeSpan; subtracting one hour from one day leaves a TimeSpan whose TotalHours is 23.

title: a temporal format pattern preserves non-specifier characters literally
rule: In a temporal pattern, every character that does not begin one of the yyyy/MM/dd/HH/mm/ss/fff specifiers is a literal, copied to the output verbatim.

title: adding past MaxValue raises OverflowException
rule: DateTime's Add* family raises OverflowException when the result falls outside MinValue..MaxValue.

title: Empty equals default(Guid)
rule: Guid.Empty is the all-zero UUID -- the same value default(Guid) produces.

title: Parse raises FormatException on a malformed string
rule: Guid.Parse(s) accepts the "D" and "N" renderings; FormatException otherwise.

title: ParseOrNull returns null for the same malformed string Parse rejects
rule: Guid.ParseOrNull(s) returns null exactly where Parse(s) raises; otherwise the parsed value.

title: FromByteArray requires exactly 16 bytes
rule: Guid.FromByteArray(bytes) requires Count = 16, raising ArgumentException otherwise.

title: new Guid(...) is rejected -- Guid declares no constructor
rule: Guid declares no constructor, so new Guid(...) is a compile error at any argument list.

title: two Random instances constructed with the same seed agree
rule: Random is seeded; constructing it with an explicit seed determines its output sequence, as distinct from the default constructor's system-time-based seed.

title: Next(maxValue) returns a value in 0..<maxValue
rule: Random.Next(maxValue) returns a value in the range 0..<maxValue.

title: Next(maxValue) rejects a negative maxValue
rule: Random.Next(maxValue) raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException when maxValue < 0.

title: Next(minValue, maxValue) rejects minValue greater than maxValue
rule: Random.Next(minValue, maxValue) raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException when minValue > maxValue.

title: a class declaring IComparable<T> must supply CompareTo
rule: IComparable<T> declares method CompareTo(other: T): int; a class whose inheritance clause lists IComparable<T> must implement it.

title: a class implementing CompareTo satisfies IComparable<T>
rule: IComparable<T> declares method CompareTo(other: T): int; a class supplying it satisfies the interface's inheritance-clause declaration.

title: CompareTo's sign convention drives a where T: IComparable<T> caller
rule: a.CompareTo(b) returns negative if a < b, zero if equal, positive if a > b; a generic caller constrained on IComparable<T>, such as Math.Min, relies on this convention to select the lesser value.

title: a record's auto-generated equality does not by itself satisfy IEquatable<T>
rule: A record conforms to an interface only when it lists that interface in its inheritance clause and declares matching members; a plain record with no such clause does not conform to IEquatable<T>, whatever equality operators it auto-generates.

title: a record listing IEquatable<T> satisfies it with no written Equals
rule: Records implement this implicitly -- once a record lists IEquatable<T> in its inheritance clause, the auto-generated Equals(T) counts as declaring the matching member, with no explicit body needed.

title: a class implements IEquatable<T> by writing Equals(T) itself
rule: classes may implement IEquatable<T> for type-safe equality without boxing -- unlike a record's synthesized member, a class supplies Equals(other: T): bool by hand.

title: user code may not implement Dispose() directly
rule: Every class implicitly implements IDisposable; user code does not implement it directly -- a class or record declaring a member named Dispose, at any parameter list, is a compile error at that declaration.

title: a destructor is the customization point for disposal, not Dispose()
rule: Every class implicitly implements IDisposable; user code does not implement it directly -- the customization points are a destructor and owned fields.

title: where T: IDisposable admits every class implicitly
rule: Every class implicitly implements IDisposable, so the constraint where T: IDisposable admits every class -- with no interface declared.

title: where T: IDisposable admits no record
rule: The constraint where T: IDisposable admits every class, no records -- records cannot implement IDisposable.

title: IAsyncDisposable is implemented explicitly with an async DisposeAsync
rule: IAsyncDisposable is implemented explicitly by classes that need asynchronous cleanup; implementations declare a method matching DisposeAsync(): Task and add async -- async never appears on the interface declaration itself. A class implementing IAsyncDisposable also declares a destructor for the synchronous fallback path.

title: Subscription, obtained from a registration call, disposes with using var
rule: Subscription has no public constructor and is obtained from a registration call, such as CancellationToken.Register; it is auto-imported, needing no explicit import statement.

title: new Subscription() is rejected -- no public constructor
rule: Subscription has no public constructor; it is obtained only from a registration call.

title: FloatToInt32Bits/Int32BitsToFloat round-trip a float exactly
rule: Int32BitsToFloat interprets the integer's bit pattern as a float; the bit patterns are preserved exactly, so FloatToInt32Bits followed by Int32BitsToFloat reproduces the original value.

title: DoubleToInt64Bits/Int64BitsToDouble round-trip a double exactly
rule: These are pure bit-reinterpretation operations: the bit patterns are preserved exactly, so DoubleToInt64Bits followed by Int64BitsToDouble reproduces the original value.

title: Reinterpret views the same bits under a different type, not a value
rule: Reinterpret copies the value's bits unchanged -- it never raises and never alters the bit pattern, unlike a value-converting cast.

title: a NaN bit pattern is preserved exactly through a round trip
rule: For NaN values, the specific bit pattern (signaling vs quiet, payload bits) is preserved -- not merely a canonical NaN value.

title: Type.Name renders the unqualified declared identifier
rule: Name renders named components unqualified — for a named non-generic type, Name is the declared identifier alone.

title: Type.FullName renders the module-qualified path
rule: FullName renders every named component qualified by its declaring module path — for a top-level type, the module then the identifier ("BankingApp.BankAccount").

title: a keyword-aliased type renders its lowercase keyword in FullName
rule: The keyword-aliased types render as their lowercase keyword in both Name and FullName ("typeof(int).FullName = \"int\""), a recorded exception to qualification.

title: a generic instantiation's FullName recurses through its arguments
rule: A generic instantiation renders the head followed by "<", its arguments joined by ", ", and ">", each argument rendered recursively in the same property's form (the document's own worked example).

title: BaseType of a class with no explicit base is the Object Type
rule: BaseType is null only for Object, interface types, value types, and function types; a class declared with no base clause still resolves a non-null BaseType, terminating the chain at Object.

title: EnumNames on a non-enum Type raises InvalidOperationException
rule: Enum metadata (EnumNames, EnumValues) is valid only when IsEnum; on any other Type, accessing either property raises InvalidOperationException.

title: a record declaring both serialization interfaces needs no body
rule: A record that declares : ISerializable and/or : IDeserializable and satisfies the synthesis-eligibility rule has the bodies generated by the compiler — the hand-written forms are unnecessary for the common case.

title: a serialized rename beginning with $ is a compile error
rule: Field names beginning with $ are reserved for the identity mapping ($id, $ref, $type, $case); a serialized "<name>" rename whose name begins with $ is a compile error at the conformance declaration.

title: a hand-written Deserialize for a value-type target returns plain T
rule: For a value-type target (a record, enum, or value-like choice) the recognized Deserialize factory returns a plain by-value T with no owned modifier.

title: owned on a value-type target's Deserialize return is rejected
rule: owned on a record, enum, or choice return is a compile error (language spec §28.1's type requirement); the recognized factory for a value-type target must not spell owned.

title: a hand-written Deserialize for a class target returns owned T
rule: The owned modifier appears exactly when the declaring type is a class — a class instance is an owned heap value transferred to the caller.

title: a class target's Deserialize without owned is rejected
rule: The owned modifier appears exactly when the declaring type is a class; a class's recognized Deserialize factory that omits owned is rejected — a plain class-typed return reads as a borrow, and a static method's borrow-shaped return of a fresh value is rejected.

title: Json.ToText / Json.Parse round-trip a value-type record
rule: Json.ToText<T> / Json.Parse<T> are defined as the corresponding agent sequence, producing and consuming the type's synthesized JSON encoding.

title: Json.Parse<T> rejects a class-typed T at compile time
rule: Parse<T> requires an IDeserializable-conforming value-type target and rejects a class-typed T at compile time, directing to ParseOwned<T>.

title: writing a non-finite float raises SerializationException
rule: WriteFloat produces a JSON number, with non-finite values (NaN, ±Infinity) raising SerializationException — JSON has no representation for them.

title: a JSON-raised SerializationException carries a null Offset
rule: SerializationException locates the fault through Offset (binary) or Line/Column (JSON); the other format's properties are null on each instance.

title: an unknown field raises SerializationException by default
rule: A field present in the input that matches no declared component is, by default (IgnoreUnknownFields = false), a SerializationException — the strict default.

title: disposing a cloned handle does not dispose the underlying value
rule: N handles jointly own one underlying value; the last handle's disposal disposes it — Clone() increments the count, and disposing one handle while another lives leaves the value alive.

title: Get() returns a borrow of the underlying value
rule: Shared<T>.Get() returns a borrow of the underlying value, sourced from the handle, valid while that handle lives.

title: Weak<T>.TryUpgrade succeeds while the value is still alive
rule: TryUpgrade returns a new strong handle if the value is still alive, null otherwise (Try shape (b)).

title: Weak<T>.TryUpgrade fails once the value has been disposed
rule: TryUpgrade returns null once the underlying value is no longer alive — Weak<T> does not keep the value alive, and after the last Shared handle disposes it, upgrading fails.

title: Shared<T> rejects a value-typed T at instantiation
rule: Shared<T> requires where T: class — proper class types only; a runtime-managed or value-typed T is rejected at instantiation.

title: TypeInitializationException.InnerException carries the original
rule: TypeInitializationException.InnerException carries the original exception that escaped the static initializer.

title: every subsequent access to a failed type raises the same exception
rule: Raised on access to a static member of a type whose static initialization failed — every subsequent access raises TypeInitializationException, not just the first.

title: integer Dn pads with leading zeros to n digits
rule: Integers admit D/Dn decimal, n = min digits, zero-padded.

title: integer X renders uppercase hex with no grouping separators
rule: Integers admit X/x hex (upper/lower), no grouping separators (no culture).

title: integer B renders binary digits
rule: Integers admit B binary.

title: floating F with no digit count defaults to 2 decimals
rule: Floating admits F/Fn fixed-point, n decimals, default 2.

title: floating P scales by 100 and appends a percent suffix
rule: Floating admits P/Pn percent (×100, % suffix).

title: decimal F2 rounds a midpoint half-to-even
rule: For a decimal operand, digit reduction under F/Fn rounds a midpoint half-to-even (banker's rounding): 0.125m under F2 renders "0.12".

title: a temporal pattern's non-specifier characters are literals
rule: In a temporal pattern, every character that does not begin one of the specifiers is a literal, copied to the output verbatim — T, Z, -, :, space, and any other non-specifier character alike.

title: a format spec on char is a compile error
rule: bool, char, string take none of the specifier vocabulary — a format spec on these is a compile error.

title: an unrecognized specifier raises FormatException
rule: The specifier vocabulary is invariant-culture only; an unrecognized specifier raises FormatException (strict-fault, as everywhere).

title: a user record conforming to INumber<T> is usable through the constraint
rule: User types conform to INumber<T> by declaring and supplying the statics; at a value conformer the operator witnesses are unmarked, matching the erased signatures.

title: char conforms to ISteppable<char> through T.Step
rule: char conforms to ISteppable<char>, witnessed by the compiler- provided conformance; ISteppable<T>.Step(value, by) advances in T's space.

title: bool conforms to none of INumber, ISteppable, IParsable
rule: bool conforms to none — deliberately: its Parse/TryParse are plain static members, not witnesses.

title: string conforms to none of INumber, ISteppable, IParsable
rule: string conforms to none of the three static abstractions — concatenation is not addition, and parsing a string to a string is meaningless.

title: a user class implementing ICollectionLiteralTarget is a literal target
rule: A user class declares exactly one of ICollectionLiteralTarget<TSelf, T> / IOwningCollectionLiteralTarget<TSelf, T>, at TSelf = itself, and supplies FromCollectionLiteral — the sequence-literal target.

title: IsOk() is true for the Ok case
rule: IsOk() distinguishes Ok from Error by case, compiler-provided.

title: Map transforms the Ok payload
rule: Map(f) maps Ok(v) to Ok(f(v)).

title: Map passes Error through unchanged
rule: Map(f) passes Error(e) through unchanged.

title: MapError transforms the Error payload
rule: MapError(f) maps Error(e) to Error(f(e)).

title: AndThen sequences a second fallible step on Ok
rule: AndThen(f) returns f(v) on Ok(v) and passes Error(e) through.

title: UnwrapOr returns the fallback on Error
rule: UnwrapOr(fallback) returns v on Ok(v) and fallback on Error(_).

title: UnwrapOr's fallback argument is evaluated eagerly
rule: UnwrapOr's argument is an ordinary value argument, not a deferred computation — it is evaluated at the call site, before the call, on the Ok path exactly as on the Error path.

title: Map is unreachable at an owning Result instantiation
rule: Map/MapError/AndThen/UnwrapOr are conditionally-admitted members, admissible only where the receiver instantiation is value-like; a borrow-bearing or owning receiver is rejected at the use site.

title: a ScopeGuard runs its action at disposal unless dismissed
rule: ScopeGuard's constructor runs the action at disposal unless dismissed.

title: Dismiss() suppresses the guard's action
rule: Dismiss() disarms the guard; after Dismiss() it is a no-op — the action does not run at disposal.

title: a ScopeGuard's action runs on the throwing edge
rule: On any throwing edge the guard's disposal runs the undo — a using var's dispose runs on the exception edge exactly as on the normal one.

title: IsDismissed defaults to False before Dismiss() is called
rule: IsDismissed exists for assertions and tests; a fresh guard is not dismissed.

title: Dismiss() is idempotent
rule: Dismiss() disarms; idempotent — a second call raises nothing.

title: Append returns this, enabling chained calls
rule: Methods return this to allow chaining; per-type Append overloads behave as Append(value.ToString()).

title: Remove raises IndexOutOfRangeException outside 0..Length
rule: Remove raises IndexOutOfRangeException when the (startIndex, length) window falls outside 0..Length.

title: Replace with an empty oldValue raises ArgumentException
rule: Replace raises ArgumentException when oldValue is empty.

title: a negative capacity raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException
rule: Negative magnitudes fault — StringBuilder(capacity) raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException when passed a negative value.

title: AppendFormat raises FormatException on a hole index outside args
rule: AppendFormat's format string contains literal text and holes {n} — n a zero-based index into args; a hole index outside args raises FormatException.

title: UTF8 round-trips GetBytes and GetString
rule: GetBytes(s: string) / GetString(bytes) form a round trip for well-formed input.

title: ASCII.GetBytes raises FormatException above U+007F
rule: ASCII is strict seven-bit; GetBytes raises FormatException on any code point above U+007F.

title: UTF8.GetString raises FormatException on malformed bytes
rule: Malformed or unrepresentable input is a defined fault — GetString raises FormatException when the input bytes are not a well-formed sequence; no replacement characters are produced.

title: UTF8.Name is "utf-8"
rule: UTF8's Name is "utf-8".

title: UTF8.GetBytes never emits a byte-order mark
rule: GetBytes never emits a byte-order mark.

title: ReadOnlyStringSpan is not borrow-bearing and may sit in a field
rule: ReadOnlyStringSpan is a deliberate exception among the spans — its only reference field is a string, so it may sit in fields and cross await.

title: Slice returns the requested sub-range
rule: Slice(start, length) constructs a new ReadOnlyStringSpan over the requested range.

title: IndexOf of an empty needle returns 0
rule: The empty span or string is a valid needle: IndexOf of an empty needle returns 0.

title: the indexer raises IndexOutOfRangeException outside 0..Length
rule: span[i] throws IndexOutOfRangeException when i < 0 or i >= Length.

title: a zero-length receiver never contains a non-empty needle
rule: A zero-length receiver is well-defined: every non-empty needle is not found — Contains returns false.

title: Array<T>.Dispose() does not dispose its stored elements
rule: Element disposal is never performed by or through a borrowing collection: a holder that owns its elements uses the owning family, whose Dispose() cascades; the borrowing family's Dispose() is a no-op.

title: Array<T>.Remove removes the borrow without disposing the element
rule: ICollection<T>'s Remove/Clear/RemoveAt on a borrowing collection remove without disposing; the element's holder, if any, keeps its disposal obligation.

title: IsReadOnly is false on a mutable borrowing collection
rule: IsReadOnly is false for every standard collection implementing ICollection<T> (Array<T>, LinkedList<T>, Set<T>, Dictionary<K, V>).

title: IList<T> is a reachable abstraction over Array<T>'s mutation surface
rule: IList<T>: IReadOnlyList<T>, ICollection<T> declares the settable indexer and Insert(index, item); Array<T> conforms to IList<T>, so a generic helper written against the interface reaches those members.

title: IOwningCollection<T>.Add takes owned and transfers ownership in
rule: IOwningCollection<T> declares method Add(owned item: T); the mutating methods of the owning family take owned parameters and take ownership of the new element.

title: IOwningCollection<T>.Clear disposes every element
rule: IOwningCollection<T> declares method Clear(); // disposes every element — the interface-level contract every owning collection shares.

title: IOwningCollection<T>.Remove disposes the removed element
rule: IOwningCollection<T> declares method Remove(item: T): bool; // disposes the removed element — the borrow-taking query removes and disposes what it finds.

title: OwningArray<string> is rejected at the instantiation site
rule: The where T: class constraint is enforced at the instantiation site: a runtime-managed reference type such as string has no disposal obligation and is rejected where the owning family requires a class or interface element type.

title: OwningArray<Widget> is admitted at a class element type
rule: The where T: class constraint on the owning family is satisfied by a concrete class type; a class-typed instantiation is admissible where a runtime-managed type is not.

title: OwningDictionary<K, V> rejects a value-typed V at instantiation
rule: OwningDictionary<K, V> requires where V: class (the value type is owned); a value-typed V has no disposal obligation and is rejected at the instantiation site, keys being unconstrained.

title: OwningLinkedList<T> rejects a function-typed T at instantiation
rule: Runtime-managed reference types (string, function values) are rejected at the owning family's instantiation site, alongside value-typed elements — ownership only makes sense for class-typed values.

title: a read-only helper accepts both a borrowing and an owning collection
rule: The two hierarchies share IEnumerable<T>, IReadOnlyCollection<T>, and IReadOnlyList<T> as common ancestors; a function that wants to read elements without taking ownership accepts one of these interfaces, and both borrowing and owning collections of T conform.

title: OwningArray<T> does not implicitly convert to Array<T>
rule: The two hierarchies do not share mutating interfaces, and there is no implicit conversion between the families — an OwningArray<T> is not an Array<T>.

title: IList<T> and IOwningList<T> are unrelated types
rule: IList<T> (borrowing) and IOwningList<T> (owning) are unrelated types with no subtyping; code that abstracts over "any mutable list" must pick one.

title: OwningArray<T> conforms to IOwningList<T>, its own mutating family
rule: The mutating interfaces do not cross families; OwningArray<T> does implement IOwningList<T>, its own family's mutable abstraction.

title: Drain() is the route from the owning family to ownership-transferring iteration
rule: For draining iteration that transfers ownership, the owning collections expose Drain() returning IOwningEnumerable<T>; default iteration stays borrowing, and the owning path is taken only at static type IOwningEnumerable<T>.

title: Array<T>(capacity) reserves storage without adding elements
rule: constructor(capacity: int); // empty (Count = 0), storage reserved

title: Array<T>(size, fill) fills every slot with the given value
rule: constructor(size: int, fill: T); // Count = size, every slot = fill (v0.165, #1375)

title: IndexOf finds the first occurrence at or after startIndex
rule: method IndexOf(item: T, startIndex: int := 0): int; // first occurrence at or after startIndex, or -1 (v0.228).

title: IndexOf with startIndex equal to Count is legal and returns -1
rule: 0 <= startIndex <= Count required, IndexOutOfRangeException otherwise; startIndex = Count is legal and returns -1.

title: IndexOf raises when startIndex exceeds Count
rule: 0 <= startIndex <= Count required, IndexOutOfRangeException otherwise.

title: Sorted() natural order requires T: IComparable<T>, checked at the call
rule: method Sorted(): owned Array<T>; // natural order; admitted only where T: IComparable<T>, checked at the call's instantiation (v0.275).

title: Sorted natural order is rejected for a non-IComparable element type
rule: The parameterless natural-order Sort/Sorted is a conditionally admitted member: admitted only where T: IComparable<T>, with the condition decided after substitution and the rejection reported at the call, never at the declaration.

title: Sorted leaves the receiver unchanged and returns a fresh copy
rule: The past-participle form (Sorted) leaves the receiver unchanged and returns a fresh owned Array<T> with the elements in the new order.

title: Sort mutates the receiver in place and returns nothing
rule: The imperative-verb form (Sort) mutates the receiver in place and returns nothing.

title: structurally mutating an Array<T> inside its own sort comparer raises
rule: Structurally mutating a collection from inside its own sort comparer raises InvalidOperationException (the loud-failure discipline, extended from enumerator invalidation to sort callbacks).

title: a fresh producer stored via Array<T>.Add warns rather than rejects
rule: On the borrowing family a fresh producer via Add/Insert/indexer-set is admitted but warns: the temporary dies at the statement's end and the stored slot dangles.

title: a fresh non-trivial-dispose element inside an Array<T> literal is a hard error
rule: For borrowing-family targets, an element expression that is a fresh producer of non-trivial-dispose class type is rejected at the literal site — the temporary would be disposed at the end of the declaration statement, leaving the collection holding a dangling borrow from birth.

title: a bound source in an Array<T> literal is admitted, unlike a fresh producer
rule: The remedy for a fresh producer inside a borrowing-family literal names the source first: bind the source to a named holder, whose borrow is then admitted at the literal site.

title: OwningArray<T>.Add transfers ownership; a fresh producer is warning-free
rule: OwningArray<T> owns each element; Add takes ownership. On the owning family a fresh producer is idiomatic and warning-free: pool.Add(new Connection("a"));

title: the OwningArray<T> indexer setter disposes the previous slot value
rule: The indexer getter produces a borrow of the slot's owned element; the setter takes ownership and disposes the previous value first — property [i: int]: T get; set(owned);

title: OwningArray<T>.RemoveAt disposes the removed element
rule: RemoveAt(index: int); // disposes the removed element

title: OwningArray<T>.Clear disposes every element
rule: Clear(); // disposes every element — the array's own Dispose() cascades the same way.

title: PopFirst takes an element out without disposing it
rule: PopFirst(): owned T; // = PopAt(0); raises if empty. Drain methods transfer ownership of elements out of the collection.

title: PopFirst raises when the array is empty
rule: PopFirst(): owned T; // = PopAt(0); raises if empty.

title: TryPopLast reports false on an empty array and assigns null
rule: TryPopLast(out owned item: T?): bool; // v0.171: the false path assigns null.

title: Drain() yields owned elements and leaves the array empty
rule: Drain(): IOwningEnumerable<T>; // iteration drains the source. A for var x in arr.Drain() do ... end loop has owned iteration variables and consumes the array's elements.

title: an undischarged owning-drain iteration variable auto-drops with the must-use warning
rule: The spec §28.3 discharge rules apply per iteration in the drain loop; an undischarged element auto-drops at the body's end with the must-use warning.

title: move arr[i] takes ownership and leaves the slot moved-from
rule: To take an element out, use PopAt(i) ... or move arr[i] (returns owned T and leaves the slot in moved-from state; the caller must reassign before the next exit point).

title: OwningArray<T>.AddRange drains its owned source argument
rule: AddRange(owned items: OwningArray<T>); // drains items into self.

title: OwningArray<T> declares no Sorted() — no owning copy is expressible
rule: OwningArray<T> declares no copy-forms of its own — no Reversed, no Sorted, no ToArray — because no owning copy is expressible: it would either double-own each element or drain the source.

title: ToArray() is reachable on OwningArray<T> as a borrowing snapshot extension
rule: What is reachable, and is not an owning copy, is the LINQ ToArray() extension on IEnumerable<T>: it resolves on an OwningArray<T> receiver and returns an owned Array<T> — a borrowing snapshot whose slots hold borrows of the elements this array still owns.

title: LinkedList<T>.AddLast returns a node borrowing the list
rule: method AddLast(item: T): LinkedListNode<T>; LinkedListNode<T> instances are owned by their containing LinkedList<T>; methods returning LinkedListNode<T> return a borrow whose lifetime is the list's lifetime.

title: LinkedList<T>.RemoveFirst removes without disposing the element
rule: LinkedList<T> is a borrowing collection (ICollection<T>); RemoveFirst/RemoveLast/RemoveNode remove without disposing, per the borrowing-family rule (spec §28.11).

title: a sequence literal constructs a LinkedList<T> in head-to-tail order
rule: A LinkedList<T> may be constructed with a sequence literal; textual order is head-to-tail: `using var l: LinkedList<int> := [10, 20, 30];` produces a list whose First is 10 and Last is 30.

title: LinkedList<T>.Add appends at the tail, equivalent to AddLast
rule: Plus the standard ICollection<T> operations: Add (appends at the tail, = AddLast — v0.195).

title: OwningLinkedList<T>.AddLast takes ownership of its argument
rule: method AddLast(owned item: T): LinkedListNode<T>; a fresh producer into the owning family is idiomatic and warning-free.

title: OwningLinkedList<T>.RemoveFirst disposes the removed element
rule: RemoveFirst(); // disposes — the owning list's removal methods dispose the element they remove.

title: OwningLinkedList<T>.PopFirst transfers ownership out without disposing
rule: To take an element out, use RemoveNode (which disposes), PopFirst / PopLast (transfer ownership to caller), or Drain().

title: OwningLinkedList<T> has no populate-from-source constructor
rule: There is no source constructor (v0.265): OwningLinkedList<T> declares constructor() and no populate-from-source form, deliberately — a borrowing source has no elements to give.

title: draining an owning array into an owning list, one element at a time
rule: Build an owning list from owned elements ... or add them one at a time, taking them out of the source as you go: for var c in src.Drain() do dst.AddLast(move c); end;

title: Dictionary<K,V> indexer raises KeyNotFoundException on a missing key
rule: Indexer dict[key] raises KeyNotFoundException if the key is not present.

title: Dictionary<K,V>.Add raises ArgumentException on a duplicate key
rule: Add(key, value) inserts and raises ArgumentException if the key is already present.

title: TryAdd reports false and makes no mutation on a duplicate key
rule: TryAdd(key, value): bool; // v0.282: false, no mutation if the key is present.

title: TryAdd leaves the existing value unchanged on a duplicate key
rule: TryAdd(key, value): bool; // false, no mutation if the key is present — the twin observation to l4_8_0003's boolean result.

title: dict[key] += 1 raises on an absent key; the compound form never inserts
rule: dict[key] += 1 desugars to a getter plus a setter, and the getter raises KeyNotFoundException on an absent key — the compound form updates, it never inserts.

title: there is no Set method on Dictionary<K,V> — writes go through the indexer
rule: There is no separate Set method — neither here nor on any other collection. A call to a Set method on any collection is rejected as an unknown member.

title: Dictionary<K,V>.Clear drops every entry without disposing keys or values
rule: Clear(); // drops every entry; disposes neither keys and values.

title: GetOrNull returns null for an absent key
rule: GetOrNull(key: K): V?; // v0.231 (§1 *OrNull tier): absent -> null.

title: a Dictionary<K,V> key type that is neither auto-hashable nor equality-declaring is rejected
rule: K must be hashable (spec §3.6/§8.3) — enforced at the instantiation site per §3.6 rule 2: a Dictionary<K, V> whose K is a record that is neither auto-hashable nor declares user equality is rejected with a diagnostic naming the property.

title: an auto-hashable record key is admitted at Dictionary<K,V>
rule: K must be hashable; an auto-hashable record — one whose storage is composed only of admissible component types — satisfies the constraint where the disqualified twin does not.

title: OwningDictionary<K,V>.Add disposes the passed value when the key is a duplicate
rule: Add(key: K, owned value: V); // ArgumentException if the key is present; the passed value was consumed at the call site and is disposed on that path (v0.195).

title: OwningDictionary<K,V>.TryAdd disposes the passed value on a duplicate key
rule: TryAdd(key: K, owned value: V): bool; // v0.282: false on duplicate, and the passed value is disposed on that path.

title: OwningDictionary<K,V>.Remove disposes the removed value
rule: Remove(key: K): bool; // disposes the removed value.

title: OwningDictionary<K,V>.Clear disposes every value
rule: Clear(); // disposes every value — the dictionary's Dispose() cascade handles the same disposal.

title: PopValue transfers ownership out without disposing
rule: PopValue(key: K): owned V; // raises if not present — the take form, in contrast with GetOrNull's look.

title: OwningDictionary<K,V> provides no default entry iteration
rule: Default for var entry in ownedDict do iteration is not provided on OwningDictionary<K, V> — the interface conformance is IDisposable only, not IOwningCollection<DictionaryEntry<K, V>>.

title: a fresh class-typed key into an OwningDictionary warns
rule: A class-typed key is held as a borrow exactly as Dictionary<K,V>'s is, and the fresh-store warning reaches that position: od[key] := v with a fresh key temporary dangles at the K8 boundary.

title: OwningDictionary<K,V>.GetOrAdd returns a borrow of the stored value
rule: GetOrAdd(key: K, factory: (K) -> owned V): V; // returns borrow — the dictionary stores the factory's value, taking ownership, and the call returns a borrow of the now-stored value.

title: Set<T>.TryAdd reports false on a duplicate element
rule: method TryAdd(item: T): bool; // returns whether added (false if duplicate).

title: OwningSet<T>.Add silently disposes the item on a duplicate
rule: When the caller passes owned item and the set already contains an equal element, Add returns () and disposes the passed-in item — the caller relinquished ownership at the call site.

title: OwningSet<T>.TryAdd disposes the passed item on a duplicate
rule: method TryAdd(owned item: T): bool; // returns whether added (false if duplicate; passed item is disposed).

title: OwningSet<T>.Pop finds the equal element and transfers ownership out
rule: Pop(query: T): owned T; // finds the equal element in the set, removes it, and returns ownership. The query and the stored element are equal by the set's Equals rule but may be distinct instances.

title: a Set<T> element type that is neither auto-hashable nor equality-declaring is rejected
rule: T must be hashable (spec §3.6/§8.3), enforced at the instantiation site per §3.6 rule 2 — same rule as Dictionary<K, V> keys.

title: OwningStack<T>.Pop transfers ownership out without disposing
rule: On the owning forms, Pop and Dequeue return ownership; the collection no longer holds the element.

title: Stack<T>.Clear drops every element and disposes nothing
rule: The borrowing forms also provide Clear(): it drops every element reference and disposes nothing, per the borrowing-family rule.

title: OwningQueue<T>.Clear disposes every element
rule: OwningStack<T>/OwningQueue<T>.Clear(); // disposes every element.

title: a Stack<T> literal is read bottom-to-top, so the last element pops first
rule: Stack<T>/OwningStack<T>: the literal lists elements bottom-to-top — the first element is pushed first (ends up at the bottom), the last element is on top (popped first). [1, 2, 3] pops 3, then 2, then 1.
