title: a Queue<T> literal places the first element at the front
rule: Queue<T>/OwningQueue<T>: the first literal element is at the front of the queue (the next to be dequeued). [1, 2, 3] dequeues 1, then 2, then 3.

title: OwningStack<T>.Peek borrows the top element without removing it
rule: pure method Peek(): T; // borrow of top element — for class T on the owning forms, Pop and Dequeue transfer ownership, while Peek only borrows.

title: IEnumerator<T>.Current is non-destructive and repeats without an intervening MoveNext
rule: IEnumerator<T>.Current is non-destructive -- it returns a borrow of the most-recently-yielded value, which the enumerator continues to own; reading it again without an intervening MoveNext yields the same value.

title: IEnumerable<T> is covariant, admitting an Array<Derived> where IEnumerable<Base> is expected
rule: IEnumerable<T> is covariant in T.

title: GetEnumerator() returns an owned IEnumerator<T> the caller must dispose
rule: GetEnumerator(): owned IEnumerator<T>; -- the caller takes ownership of the returned enumerator and must dispose it.

title: a second TakeCurrent without an intervening advance raises InvalidOperationException
rule: A second take without an intervening advance, or a take before the first advance/after exhaustion, raises InvalidOperationException.

title: TakeCurrent before the first advance raises InvalidOperationException
rule: A take before the first advance/after exhaustion raises InvalidOperationException.

title: an advanced-but-untaken element is disposed when the enumerator is disposed
rule: Between a successful advance and TakeCurrent() the enumerator owns the pending value -- a Dispose() after an advance whose value was never taken disposes it; an advanced-but-untaken element neither leaks nor reaches the consumer.

title: an undischarged owned for-loop variable over an owning source auto-drops with a warning
rule: A for var x in src do ... end where src is an IOwningEnumerable<T> produces owned iteration variables; where the body does not discharge x, the affine auto-drop disposes it at the iteration's scope end with the plain-var must-use warning.

title: disposing a drain-view frame does not dispose the collection; partial iteration leaves the remainder
rule: Every owning collection's Drain() mints a fresh drain-view frame -- a caller-owned enumerable over the collection, never the collection re-exposed -- so the frame's disposal at loop end never disposes the collection, and partial iteration leaves the undrained remainder in place.

title: a fresh GetOwningEnumerator() on a live drain view continues over the current remainder
rule: Each GetOwningEnumerator() call on a live view yields a fresh enumerator over the collection's current remainder -- a re-enumeration continues draining what remains, never replaying what already left.

title: a Span<T> may not outlive the OwningBuffer<T> source it borrows
rule: A borrow-bearing record value may not outlive the source of any borrow it contains; a Span<T>'s Buffer field carries a borrow of the OwningBuffer<T> it views, bounded by the source's lifetime.

title: a Span<T> is usable while its OwningBuffer<T> source stays live
rule: A borrow-bearing record value is admitted while the source of every borrow it contains is still live; Span<T> reads through the buffer for as long as the buffer is not disposed.

title: a Span<T> may not be constructed from an unbound temporary buffer
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be constructed from a temporary bound to one of its borrow-carrying fields -- a fresh call result not bound to a named location has a lifetime ending at the construction expression, so the record would immediately outlive that source.

title: a Span<T> constructed from a named, bound buffer is admitted
rule: Bind the source to a named local whose scope outlives the record, and pass that -- the remedy for the no-temporary-source rule.

title: a Span<T> may not be stored in an instance field of a class
rule: A borrow-bearing record value may not be stored in an instance field of a class -- a class instance's lifetime is not bounded by any borrow source's scope, and the store is rejected statically.

title: a Span<T> may not be stored in a static field unless it is the null-source form
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a static field of any type, except when every reference-typed field of the value is null; Span<T>'s Buffer field is a non-nullable reference, so no Span<T> value ever satisfies the null-source form.

title: OwningBuffer<T>'s indexer setter disposes the slot's previous value at class T
rule: The indexer's setter takes ownership of the assigned value and disposes whatever the slot previously held.

title: a slot moved-from via move buf[i] must be restored before the enclosing scope exits
rule: move buf[i] leaves the slot moved-from; the field-restoration rule of language spec 28.8.1 applies -- any slot moved-from must be reassigned before any exit edge, because auto-dispose on a moved-from slot is not defined.

title: the natural restoration for a moved-from nullable slot is assigning null
rule: move buf[i] is admitted and produces an owned T? value, leaving the slot in moved-from state; the natural restoration for a nullable slot is buf[i] := null.

title: move buf[i] is not admitted for value-typed T
rule: For value-typed T, move buf[i] is not admitted -- values have no ownership to transfer, and are read with the plain indexer instead.

title: ReadOnlySpan<T> has no ToArray() member
rule: ReadOnlySpan<T> declared ToArray(): owned Array<T> from v0.222 until v0.277, which deleted it; the compiler never admitted the call, and the absence is now recorded -- there is no materializer on this family.

title: TryReadInt16LittleEndian returns false and leaves value default on a short span
rule: Read methods throw IndexOutOfRangeException if the span is shorter than the type being read; TryRead* variants return false instead of throwing and assign the out parameter to default(T) on the false path.

title: OwningBuffer<T> does not admit a runtime-managed reference type such as string
rule: What is not admitted. Runtime-managed reference types (string, function types) are not admitted as T -- they have no disposal obligation, so the owning semantics add nothing.

title: move is not admitted through an ArraySpan<T> indexer for any T
rule: move arrSpan[i] is not admitted for any T -- borrowed slots have no ownership to transfer; the plain indexer-get is the only read form.

title: writing through an ArraySpan<T> stores a borrow with no disposal of the previous slot
rule: For class T, the assigned value is a borrow -- no ownership transfer; the previous slot contents are not disposed (they were borrows, not owned values). This differs from Span<T>'s class-T setter.

title: an ArraySpan<T> may not be constructed from an unbound temporary array
rule: A borrow-bearing record may not be constructed from a temporary bound to one of its borrow-carrying fields; ArraySpan<T>'s Source field carries a borrow of the Array<T>, so a fresh unbound array is rejected.

title: an ArraySpan<T> constructed from a named, bound array is admitted
rule: Bind the source to a named local whose scope outlives the record, and pass that -- the remedy for the no-temporary-source rule, applied to the Array<T>-backed span family.

title: ArraySpan<T>.Fill assigns the value to every slot, for class and value T alike
rule: Unlike Span<T> (whose mutation API splits by T's category), ArraySpan<T> provides a single uniform mutation surface for all T -- admissible because Array<T> slots do not own their contents.

title: neither ArraySpan<T> nor ReadOnlyArraySpan<T> declares ToArray()
rule: No ToArray() on either span family -- neither materializes; a view on this side is over an Array<T>, which already carries ToArray() and Slice, so materialization is reachable through the source instead.

title: SequenceEqual on the interface admits cross-source comparison between span families
rule: SequenceEqual is on the interface, with parameter type IReadOnlySpan<TElement> -- this admits cross-source equality: a ReadOnlySpan<byte> can be compared against a ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>.

title: Slice is deliberately not a member of IReadOnlySpan<TElement>
rule: The interface deliberately omits Slice -- each concrete span type has its own Slice returning the same concrete type, and putting Slice on the interface would propagate the interface-typed handle.

title: a concrete span passed as IReadOnlySpan<TElement> is boxed call-bounded and reads through it
rule: A span passed as an IReadOnlySpan<TElement> parameter is boxed per the standard rule for borrow-bearing records; the interface parameter admits any span whose source outlives the call frame.

title: an IReadOnlySpan<TElement> parameter may not be stored in a field that outlives the call
rule: A method declaring IReadOnlySpan<TElement> cannot store the parameter in a field that outlives the call -- the standard borrow-bearing-record constraints; nothing new is added by the interface.

title: SortedDictionary<K, V> iterates entries in ascending key order regardless of insertion order
rule: A comparison-ordered associative collection: iteration visits entries in ascending key order.

title: Add on a present key raises ArgumentException
rule: method Add(key: K, value: V); // v0.282: ArgumentException if the key is present -- the duplicate-is-a-bug tier.

title: TryAdd on a present key returns false and does not mutate
rule: method TryAdd(key: K, value: V): bool; // v0.282 (shape (d)): false and no mutation if present.

title: FirstKey on an empty SortedDictionary raises InvalidOperationException
rule: pure readonly property FirstKey: K; // least key; InvalidOperationException if empty.

title: the indexer get raises KeyNotFoundException on an absent key
rule: property [key: K]: V; // get: KeyNotFoundException if absent.

title: structurally modifying a SortedDictionary during iteration raises InvalidOperationException
rule: Iteration is O(n) in ascending key order, one live pass at a time; structural modification during iteration raises InvalidOperationException.

title: SortedSet<T> iterates in ascending order regardless of insertion order
rule: A comparison-ordered set: membership by CompareTo-equality, iteration in ascending order.

title: Add on an already-present element is a silent no-op
rule: As with Set<T>, adding an equal element leaves the set unmodified -- Add returns () and discards silently.

title: TryAdd on an already-present element returns false
rule: method TryAdd(item: T): bool; // false if an equal item is present.

title: First on an empty SortedSet raises InvalidOperationException
rule: pure readonly property First: T; // least; InvalidOperationException if empty.

title: FrozenArray<T>.From(owned buffer) steals a value-typed buffer's storage
rule: static method From(owned buffer: OwningBuffer<T>): owned FrozenArray<T>; // VALUE-TYPED T ONLY: O(1) -- steals the storage; the buffer is consumed.

title: FrozenArray<T>.From(items) copies and is the only construction form for string
rule: static method From(items: Array<T>): owned FrozenArray<T>; // Copies; the only construction form for T = string.

title: FrozenArray<T> has no indexer setter -- deeply immutable after construction
rule: public property [i: int]: T get; end; -- FrozenArray<T> declares no mutating member, so no writer can exist after construction.

title: freezing a buffer with a live span local over it is rejected by the consume-site freeze
rule: A live local of borrow-bearing record type counts as a live local borrow of every held borrow's source: var s := buf.AsSpan(); freezes buf against FrozenArray<T>.From(move buf) -- and every other consume -- for as long as s is live, a borrow being live at a consume site when some path from the site reaches a later use of it.

title: ToArray() returns a fresh mutable copy out of a FrozenArray<T>
rule: method ToArray(): owned Array<T>; // fresh mutable copy back out.

title: a static owned readonly FrozenArray<T> is a sound all-domains singleton
rule: A static owned readonly FrozenArray<T> is a sound all-domains singleton and draws no language spec 22.12 rule-4 warning (rule 4's warning-suppression set, the v0.186 ruling); mutable statics of it remain rejected.

title: Increment on an absent key creates it at delta
rule: method Increment(key: K, delta: int := 1); // absent key is created at delta.

title: CountOf returns 0 for an absent key
rule: method CountOf(key: K): int; // 0 when absent.

title: Contains distinguishes a present-at-zero key from an absent one
rule: method Contains(key: K): bool; // distinguishes present-at-zero from absent; enables key in tally.

title: a key decremented to zero or below is not removed and still counts toward Count
rule: A key decremented to zero or below is not removed -- it keeps its position, counts toward Count, and CountOf returns its possibly negative value; only Remove deletes it.

title: Counter<K> iterates its entries in insertion order
rule: Counter<K> implements IEnumerable<DictionaryEntry<K, int>>; iteration is insertion-ordered, exactly as Dictionary.

title: Increment on an existing key updates in place and preserves its insertion position
rule: Increment on an existing key updates in place and preserves its position.

title: Insert mints a handle, GetOrNull reads the stored value as a borrow, and the map's disposal cascades
rule: Insert(owned value: T): SlotHandle takes ownership and mints a handle; GetOrNull(handle) returns a borrow of the stored value when the handle is live; disposing the map disposes every value it still holds.

title: Remove disposes the value and the handle reads absent afterwards
rule: Remove(handle) disposes the value and returns true; a handle whose slot has been vacated reads as absent — Contains is false and GetOrNull is null — for the rest of the map's life.

title: a stale handle after slot reuse reads absent while the new handle for the same slot reads live
rule: Insert reuses the most recently vacated slot; a handle is live iff its slot holds a value and the slot's generation equals the handle's Generation, so a handle minted before the slot was vacated never reads a later occupant of its slot.
check: all:disposed a\nFalse True False True\ndisposed b

title: Clear disposes every value in descending Index and keeps the map usable
rule: Clear() disposes every value in descending Index and keeps the emptied map.

title: disposing the map disposes its values in descending Index
rule: The map's own Dispose() disposes the values in descending Index — the ordered families' reverse-storage-order rule of spec §28.11, storage order here being slot order — then releases the storage.

title: Drain yields owned values in ascending Index and vacates each slot as it goes
rule: Drain() returns an IOwningEnumerable<T> whose iteration transfers each value to the consumer in ascending Index and vacates its slot; after full iteration the map is empty.

title: a handle minted by another map raises ArgumentException
rule: Every handle-taking member raises ArgumentException when the handle was minted by a different OwningSlotMap<T> instance — a caller bug, not an expected absence.

title: an unmarked read of an owned binding at Insert's owned position is rejected
rule: Insert(owned value: T) takes ownership: a fresh producer or a moved binding, never an unmarked read of an owned binding (spec §28.3 K3.3 — an owned argument is spelled `move x` at the call site).

title: a moved owned binding at Insert's owned position compiles warning-free
rule: Insert(owned value: T) takes ownership: a fresh producer or a moved binding is admitted, and the moved binding needs no other discharge.

title: Dispose through the borrow GetOrNull returns is rejected
rule: Get, GetOrNull and TryGetValue produce borrows sourced from the map; disposing through such a borrow is spec §28.6's compile error — the map owns the value, and Remove/PopValue are the forms that release it.

title: default(SlotHandle) denotes a slot of no map and raises ArgumentException
rule: A default(SlotHandle) (spec §17.11) denotes a slot of no map and takes the same fault as a handle minted by a different OwningSlotMap<T> instance: every handle-taking member raises ArgumentException — no map ever mints it.

title: Where's predicate is not invoked until the query is enumerated
rule: All are lazy unless documented otherwise. Callback retention: a predicate passed to a lazy operator is retained by the returned query value until enumeration, not invoked at the call.

title: a bound lazy query enumerated twice is a compile error
rule: A lazy query is single-consumption -- it may be enumerated at most once; a second enumeration is a compile error where the flow analysis can see it statically.

title: passing a query as an IEnumerable<T> argument transfers its single-enumeration right
rule: Passing the query as an IEnumerable<T> argument transfers the single-enumeration right to the callee; inside a callee a plain IEnumerable<T> parameter is statically untracked, so a re-enumeration there is enforced only by the runtime InvalidOperationException guard.

title: composing a further deferred operator spends the source query's enumeration right
rule: Applying a further deferred operator (var q2 := q.Select(f);) spends the binding q's enumeration right -- using q afterwards as a query is a static error where visible.

title: materializing with ToArray() produces a result that may be enumerated more than once
rule: To enumerate the results more than once, materialize first -- using var ys := xs.Where(...).ToArray(); produces an owned Array<T>, which, like any collection, may be enumerated any number of times.

title: Take clamps a negative count to zero
rule: Take/Skip clamp -- a negative count behaves as 0, and a count beyond the source takes everything / skips everything; they are range operations, not magnitude constructors.

title: Zip ends when either input sequence ends
rule: Zip ends when either input ends.

title: an OrderBy result mints a single-consumption frame by its lazy-query kind
rule: Each deferred operator call mints a caller-owned query frame; where the declared type is one of stdlib section 5's derived interfaces instead (the OrderBy/OrderByDescending/ThenBy/ThenByDescending quartet's IOrderedEnumerable<T>), the operator is the same minting member by its lazy-query kind.

title: OrderBy composed with ThenBy is stable at every tier
rule: The OrderBy family is STABLE; ThenBy/ThenByDescending break ties left by the preceding key while preserving encounter order among equal elements.

title: ToDictionary raises ArgumentException on a duplicate key
rule: ToDictionary (both overloads) raises ArgumentException on a duplicate key -- Dictionary.Add semantics; silent last-wins would mask a defective key selector.

title: GroupBy materializes fully on its first enumeration, one key-selector call per element
rule: GroupBy is lazy until its first enumeration, then materializes fully -- no complete group can exist before the source is exhausted, so the operator buffers.

title: Sum() accumulates in the element's own type and is overflow-checked in it
rule: Sum now returns the element's own type, so a narrow integer element type accumulates in that type and is overflow-checked in it -- bytes.Sum() over an Array<byte> raises OverflowException past 255.

title: Sum() on an empty source returns the zero of its result type
rule: Sum without a selector is the constrained generic; on an empty source Sum (both forms) returns the zero of its result type.

title: Min() on an empty source raises InvalidOperationException
rule: Min and Max without a selector are generic over comparable types; Min()/Max() -- selector and no-selector forms alike -- throw InvalidOperationException on an empty source.

title: MinOrNull() on an empty source returns null
rule: method MinOrNull(): T?; // null if empty.

title: CancellationTokenSource.IsCancellationRequested agrees with its Token's property
rule: CancellationTokenSource.IsCancellationRequested and source.Token.IsCancellationRequested always return the same value: the source's property is a convenience equivalent to source.Token.IsCancellationRequested.

title: Register on an already-cancelled token fires the callback synchronously
rule: If the token is already in the cancelled state at the moment Register is called, the callback is invoked synchronously on the calling thread before Register returns.

title: ThrowIfCancellationRequested raises OperationCanceledException once cancelled
rule: Cancellation surfaces as OperationCanceledException (language spec §30.8); the generated async iterator's implicit token.ThrowIfCancellationRequested() "faults the in-flight MoveNextAsync task with OperationCanceledException" on a requested cancellation (language spec §30.7), which is the call's own effect.

title: Register on a published static source raises InvalidOperationException
rule: A source is published at a static readonly field of the type; on a published source, Register raises InvalidOperationException.

title: CancellationToken.None is never cancelled and never raises
rule: CancellationToken.None has no source and is never in the cancelled state, so ThrowIfCancellationRequested never raises on it.

title: Register on an unpublished source invokes the callback on Cancel
rule: Register invokes the callback when cancellation is requested; the returned Subscription removes the registration when disposed.

title: disposing a source performs a full Cancel before severing registrations
rule: Disposal performs a full Cancel() (v0.195): registered callbacks that have not yet run are invoked synchronously on the disposing thread before the registration list is severed.

title: a parent already cancelled at creation cancels the linked source at once
rule: A parent already cancelled at creation cancels the linked source before CreateLinked returns — the same race-free synchronous policy as Register on a cancelled token.

title: cancelling a parent cancels the linked source
rule: The linked source enters the cancelled state when any parent token cancels or its own Cancel()/CancelAfter() fires, whichever happens first.

title: Register on a linked child of a published parent raises
rule: A linked child of a published parent is published; on a published source, Register raises InvalidOperationException.

title: TryAcquire succeeds immediately on an uncontended Mutex
rule: TryAcquire(timeout) returns owned Lock? — an owned Lock on success or null on timeout.

title: TryAcquire(TimeSpan.Zero) returns null while the mutex is already held
rule: TryAcquire(timeout) returns owned Lock? — an owned Lock on success or null on timeout (§6.2). Mutex is non-reentrant — "a holder re-acquiring waits on itself, whatever the acquisition form" — is language spec §30.12's sentence, not §6.2's.

title: Semaphore.TryAcquire fails once the permit count is exhausted
rule: constructor(initialCount: int); ... TryAcquire(timeout: TimeSpan): owned SemaphoreToken?

title: releasing a SemaphoreToken restores a permit for the next Acquire
rule: SemaphoreToken — destructor; // releases the held permit

title: Atomic<T>.Exchange atomically replaces Value and returns the previous value
rule: Exchange(value) atomically replaces Value with value and returns the previous value.

title: AtomicInteger<T>.Increment returns the post-increment value
rule: Increment(): T; // returns post-increment value

title: AtomicInteger<T>.Add raises OverflowException on overflow
rule: Increment, Decrement, and Add perform the operation atomically ... an operation whose mathematical result is not representable in T raises OverflowException.

title: Subscribe then Raise invokes the handler with the payload
rule: Subscribe registers a handler and returns an owned Subscription; Raise invokes handlers in subscription order.

title: Raise with zero subscribers is a no-op
rule: With zero subscribers, both methods are no-ops — no null check, no ?., no Invoke indirection.

title: a synchronous handler exception stops later handlers — first error wins
rule: If a synchronous handler throws, subsequent handlers are not invoked and the exception propagates out of Raise to the raiser.

title: SharedEventSource.Subscribe rejects a capturing handler
rule: Every subscribe position of the pair admits only capture-free handlers — a non-capturing lambda or a static method reference.

title: SharedEventSource.Subscribe accepts a capture-free handler
rule: Every subscribe position of the pair admits only capture-free handlers — a non-capturing lambda or a static method reference.

title: Raise invokes handlers in subscription order
rule: Raise and RaiseAsync invoke handlers in subscription order, over a snapshot of the subscriber list taken when the raise begins.

title: a handler subscribing during a raise affects only the next raise
rule: Raise invokes handlers over a snapshot of the subscriber list taken when the raise begins (v0.163): a handler that subscribes or unsubscribes during the raise affects the next raise, never the in-flight pass.

title: disposing the Subscription removes the handler
rule: Subscribe registers a handler and returns an owned Subscription; disposing the subscription removes the handler.

title: the producer-side += form registers a handler on the readonly source field
rule: The producer-side `_clicked += h` spelling remains available on the `readonly` field because the subscription forms neither read nor assign the operand; `lhs += h` rewrites to `lhs.Add(h)`.

title: EventSource of unit provides a no-argument Raise overload
rule: No-payload events use `EventSource<()>`; both `EventSource<()>` and `SharedEventSource<()>` provide a convenience `Raise()` overload that takes no arguments, equivalent to `Raise(())`.

title: RaiseAsync awaits each handler's task before invoking the next
rule: RaiseAsync returns a Task that completes when every handler's task completes; each handler's task is awaited before the next is invoked.

title: a faulted async handler stops later handlers and propagates from RaiseAsync
rule: If an asynchronous handler's task faults, subsequent handlers are not invoked and the exception propagates from the awaited RaiseAsync.

title: a cancelled async handler task behaves exactly as a fault
rule: If an asynchronous handler's task is cancelled, the behavior is the same as a fault: subsequent handlers are not invoked and OperationCanceledException propagates from the awaited RaiseAsync.

title: the source classes are invariant in their payload type
rule: The source classes are invariant — `Raise(payload: T)` places T in input position; an exposed source is simply invariant, as its signature dictates.

title: a covariant IEvent face over a narrower source is directly declarable
rule: IEvent<T> and IAsyncEvent<T> are covariant in T (`out T`). Covariant exposure is directly declarable by the pattern: an EventSource<Dog> field behind a `property Sightings: IEvent<Animal>` face.

title: SharedEventSource does not implement IEvent
rule: SharedEventSource<T> deliberately does not implement IEvent<T> — an upcast would launder the capture-free requirement through IEvent<T>.Subscribe's capture-admitting `scoped` signature.

title: the ISharedEvent face subscribes and receives a raise
rule: SharedEventSource<T> implements ISharedEvent<T>, whose Subscribe admits a capture-free handler and returns an owned Subscription; Raise is a synchronized snapshot-raise whose handlers run on the raising domain.

title: a handler capturing a constructor parameter other than this is rejected
rule: A captured constructor parameter other than `this` is not admitted where it contributes a borrow source (spec §28.3) — a class-, interface- or plain function-typed parameter, or an `owned` one: such a parameter is a borrow of a caller local and does not provably outlive the constructed object (v0.301).

title: a handler capturing this is admitted when the Subscription is an owned field
rule: Storing a Subscription in an owned field of `this` resolves the bounding object to `this` (spec §28.14 form 3), so a handler capturing `this` (or state reached through it) is admitted regardless of how the publisher was reached.

title: instantiating TaskCompletionSource<T> with a class T is rejected
rule: For non-class T (copyable value types, string, runtime-managed reference types). Instantiating with a class T is a compile error pointing to OwningTaskCompletionSource<T>.

title: OwningTaskCompletionSource<T> is the admitted spelling for a class T
rule: For class T. Result is transferred via `owned` parameter; produced task is Pattern B. OwningTaskCompletionSource<T> where T: class.

title: SetException's owned exception is re-raised to the awaiter
rule: Fault-path ownership (v0.179). SetException/TrySetException (all forms) take the exception owned: the produced task becomes the single owner of its fault exception (awaiters borrow it on re-raise).

title: disposing the source before completion faults the produced task
rule: destructor; // disposes the produced task, faulting it first if the source is disposed before completion.

title: a caught exception borrow cannot feed SetException's owned parameter
rule: A caller that holds only a caught borrow (spec §31.1) constructs a fresh cause-chained exception instead: tcs.SetException(new Exception(ex.Message, ex));

title: a fresh cause-chained exception is the admitted spelling from a catch arm
rule: A caller that holds only a caught borrow (spec §31.1) constructs a fresh cause-chained exception instead: tcs.SetException(new Exception(ex.Message, ex));

title: WhenAny yields the index of the first task to settle and never re-raises its fault
rule: WhenAny(tasks: Array<Task>): Task<int>; // index of the first task to SETTLE — success, fault, or cancellation; never re-raises the winner's fault (inspect tasks[i]).

title: the owning WhenAll overload produces an owned array holding each task's result
rule: Task.WhenAll<T>(owned tasks: OwningArray<OwningTask<T>>): OwningTask<OwningArray<T>> where T: class — aggregates OwningTask<T> results into an owned array of owned elements.

title: Spawn's value-typed result crosses the join as a plain Task<R>
rule: Spawn<R>(entry: () -> R): owned Task<R> where R: sendable, notnull; // Value-typed or string result (Pattern A).

title: Spawn's class-typed result transfers ownership to the awaiter
rule: Class-typed result: ownership transfers to the awaiter (Pattern B). Spawn<R>(entry: () -> owned R): owned OwningTask<R> where R: sendable, class;

title: a fault in the entry surfaces at the join as DomainFaultedException
rule: DomainFaultedException ... Message carries the original exception's message text.

title: CancellationToken cannot cross a domain boundary as a spawn argument
rule: A CancellationToken never crosses a domain boundary itself: it is a borrow-bearing record and not sendable.

title: a sendable value type crosses the spawn boundary as a copy
rule: A CancellationToken never crosses a domain boundary itself: it is a borrow-bearing record and not sendable.

title: T must be sendable; a non-sendable class T is rejected
rule: T must be sendable; the instantiation is rejected otherwise (language spec §3.6).

title: a sealed class with sendable fields admits Channel<T>
rule: T must be sendable; the instantiation is rejected otherwise (language spec §3.6).

title: items from one sender are received in per-sender FIFO order
rule: Ordering. Per-sender FIFO; cross-sender interleaving is an unspecified consistent total order; each item is received exactly once.

title: after the last sender closes, drained receives raise ChannelClosedException
rule: Closing. Disposing the last sender closes the channel; buffered items remain receivable, and after the drain Receive raises ChannelClosedException.

title: Close() from the receiving end is idempotent
rule: Close() is idempotent: on an already-closed channel it is a no-op, and later sender disposals remain no-ops with respect to the closed state.

title: TryReceive returns false for both empty-open and drained-closed; IsClosed distinguishes
rule: TryReceive returns false for both empty-open and drained-closed; consult IsClosed to distinguish.

title: synchronous Send on a full bounded channel raises ChannelFullException
rule: on a FULL bounded channel raises ChannelFullException (v0.174); ChannelClosedException if closed

title: ReceiveAll completes normally on drained-and-closed
rule: ReceiveAll() ... suspends while empty-and-open, and completes the enumeration normally on drained-and-closed — ChannelClosedException stops being control flow for the normal exit.

title: disposing the channel disposes undelivered items in reverse insertion order
rule: Disposing the Channel<T> closes it immediately and disposes every undelivered class-typed item in reverse insertion order; subsequent Send raises ChannelClosedException.

title: a mutable static Channel<T> field is rejected
rule: A mutable static Channel<T> field is rejected by language spec §22.12 rule 2 (v0.181).

title: a static readonly Channel<T> draws rule 4's confinement warning
rule: a static readonly Channel<T> draws rule 4's warning: the channel object is the single-consumer receiving end and must stay confined to one consuming domain.

title: Send on a closed channel raises ChannelClosedException
rule: Send(owned item: T); ... ChannelClosedException if closed.

title: disposing a pending Receive task deregisters without consuming an item
rule: Disposing a Receive task before an item has been dequeued into it deregisters the waiter; no message is consumed or lost — the next item goes to the next receive.

title: TaskScope may not be bound with a plain using var
rule: Consumption is await using only — a plain using var, or dropping the scope undisposed, is a compile error naming this rule: a synchronous destructor cannot await the drain.

title: await using is the admitted way to consume a TaskScope
rule: Consumption is await using only — a plain using var, or dropping the scope undisposed, is a compile error naming this rule.

title: await Join() is mandatory on the normal path
rule: await Join() is mandatory on the normal path (compile error where provable, InvalidOperationException from DisposeAsync otherwise): the join-and-re-raise happens at a source-visible await, never at an unmarked end.

title: an await Join() call in the method body satisfies the mandatory-join rule
rule: await Join() is mandatory on the normal path (compile error where provable, InvalidOperationException from DisposeAsync otherwise).

title: a child's fault re-raises at await Join()
rule: await Join(): Task; // await all children; re-raise the FIRST fault (first-fault-wins, no aggregation)

title: Spawn after the scope has closed raises InvalidOperationException
rule: Spawn after close (after Join returned or disposal began) raises InvalidOperationException — deterministic, never a silent extension of the drain.

title: Spawn admits a capture-bearing body bounded by the scope
rule: method Spawn(scoped body: () -> Task); // start a child (§28.14 storage-bounded)

title: a borrowing collection of class elements cannot be a Locked<T> interior
rule: borrowing collections of class elements do not (Locked<Dictionary<string, Session>> is rejected — own the values: Locked<OwningDictionary<string, Session>>).

title: an owning collection of sendable elements is an admitted Locked<T> interior
rule: owning collections of sendable elements (OwningDictionary, OwningSet, …) ... qualify ... Locked<OwningDictionary<string, Session>> is the admitted spelling.

title: a lock guard's Value is a mutable borrow of the interior
rule: A guard's Value property is a borrow of the interior whose source is the guard ... so the borrow rules bound every interior borrow by the guard's life.

title: TryLock(timeout) returns null while the lock is already held
rule: TryLock(timeout: TimeSpan): owned LockGuard<T>?; // null on timeout (Try shape (b)). Non-reentrant: a holder re-acquiring waits on itself.

title: an explicit Dispose() of a live guard binding is rejected while a borrow of its Value is live
rule: a guard binding cannot be explicitly Dispose()d or discarded while a borrow from its Value is live.

title: disposing a guard after its last interior borrow use is admitted
rule: a guard binding cannot be explicitly Dispose()d or discarded while a borrow from its Value is live.

title: a static owned readonly Locked<T> registry compiles warning-free
rule: The canonical process-global registry — the static owned readonly idiom (rule-4 warning suppressed by §22.12 rule 4's warning-suppression set, the v0.186 ruling).

title: a store through a ReadGuard-sourced borrow is rejected
rule: In the body holding the guard, the compiler rejects all stores, move, and ref/out passing through a ReadGuard-sourced borrow.

title: a WriteGuard's Value carries no store restriction
rule: WriteGuard<T>.Value and LockGuard<T>.Value carry no restriction — those guards are exclusive.

title: a write guard's mutation is observed by a later read acquisition
rule: public method Read(): owned ReadGuard<T>; ... public method Write(): owned WriteGuard<T>;

title: Map reassembles results in input order
rule: Results in input order; first fault wins, surfaced at the await as DomainFaultedException.

title: Reduce over an associative combiner with an identity seed matches the serial fold
rule: The serial-fold correspondence holds exactly when the combiner is associative and the seed is its identity.

title: a capturing lambda body is rejected as a Parallel spawn position
rule: The body/selector/combiner parameters are spawn positions: capture-free (a non-capturing lambda or a static method reference).

title: a capture-free lambda is an admitted Parallel spawn position
rule: The body/selector/combiner parameters are spawn positions: capture-free (a non-capturing lambda or a static method reference).

title: ForEach invokes its body exactly once per element
rule: public static method ForEach<A>(items: Array<A>, body: (A) -> (), degree: int := 0): owned Task where A: sendable, notnull;

title: Stream has no async Span<byte> overload — only the windowed Array<byte> async form exists
rule: No async span overloads (v0.179, #1438). Asynchronous byte I/O uses the heap-owned windowed form — ReadAsync/WriteAsync(buffer: Array<byte>, offset, count, token); the async span overloads were removed.

title: FileStream(path, mode) resolves via the FileAccess.ReadWrite default
rule: access defaults to FileAccess.ReadWrite: new FileStream(path, mode) is new FileStream(path, mode, FileAccess.ReadWrite).

title: File.WriteAllBytes accepts a ReadOnlySpan<byte> for the zero-copy serializer path
rule: public static method WriteAllBytes(path: string, contents: ReadOnlySpan<byte>); // v0.165 (#1358): serializer-output path, zero-copy

title: Directory.Delete(path) resolves via the recursive := false default
rule: public static method Delete(path: string, recursive: bool := false); // IOException if non-empty and not recursive

title: Path.GetExtension returns "" when the path has no extension
rule: GetExtension(path): string; // "" when none

title: catching FileNotFoundException requires `import System.IO;`
rule: None are auto-imported; users import System.IO; to get them.

title: FileNotFoundException is unresolved without `import System.IO;`
rule: None are auto-imported; users import System.IO; to get them.

title: Reset() stops the stopwatch
rule: Reset() stops the stopwatch and zeroes Elapsed; a restart from zero is sw.Reset(); sw.Start();

title: StartNew() returns an already-running Stopwatch
rule: static method StartNew(): owned Stopwatch; ... StartNew() is the fresh-instance form.

title: Debug.Assert never throws — a true condition just continues
rule: Assert never throws; a failed assertion terminates the process, so a true condition simply continues execution.

title: int.Parse raises FormatException on non-numeric input
rule: The ParseOrNull note fixes Parse's own contract: absence of a valid integer literal in the input raises FormatException (the FormatException/OverflowException contract Parse establishes).

title: int.TryParse returns false and assigns default(int) on failure
rule: TryParse(s: string, out result: int): bool is Try shape (c) — false on failure, with the out slot assigned default(T) (here 0).

title: int.ParseOrNull returns null exactly where Parse raises
rule: ParseOrNull(s: string): int? — null exactly where Parse(s) raises (the FormatException/OverflowException contract); otherwise the parsed value.

title: int.MinValue and int.MaxValue are the exact compiler-provided constants
rule: public static const MinValue: int := -2_147_483_648; public static const MaxValue: int := 2_147_483_647;

title: int.Parse(s, radix) parses under the requested radix
rule: static pure method Parse(s: string, radix: int): int; radix in {2, 8, 10, 16}.

title: int.Parse with an unsupported radix raises ArgumentException
rule: radix in {2, 8, 10, 16}; any other radix raises ArgumentException — a caller bug, not input failure.

title: int.Parse raises OverflowException on an out-of-range value
rule: Parse establishes the FormatException/OverflowException contract that ParseOrNull and TryParse are defined against.

title: double.IsNaN reports the NaN constant true
rule: static pure method IsNaN(value: double): bool;

title: double.IeeeEquals(NaN, NaN) is false
rule: IeeeEquals returns false for any pair involving NaN, including NaN-vs-NaN.

title: Decimal.Round uses banker's rounding (round-half-to-even) at a midpoint
rule: pure method Round(digits: int): decimal; // banker's rounding (round-half-to-even), matching Math.Round.

title: Decimal.Round raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException outside 0..28 digits
rule: Round(digits: int): decimal; digits outside 0..28: ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

title: decimal.ParseOrNull returns null exactly where Parse raises
rule: ParseOrNull(s: string): decimal? — v0.231: null exactly where Parse(s) raises; otherwise the parsed value.

title: bool.Parse is case-insensitive
rule: static pure method Parse(s: string): bool; // "true"/"false", case-insensitive

title: bool.ToString renders exactly "True" or "False"
rule: pure method ToString(): string; // "True" or "False"

title: char.Parse raises FormatException on a multi-code-point string
rule: Parse accepts a string containing exactly one code point (s.Length = 1); any other input — the empty string or a multi-code-point string — raises FormatException.

title: char.IsDigit classifies a decimal digit
rule: static pure method IsDigit(c: char): bool;

title: Split keeps every empty segment between separator occurrences
rule: Splitting yields every (possibly empty) segment between separator occurrences: adjacent separators yield an empty element between them. There is no remove-empty-entries option.

title: IndexOf("") is 0 — the vacuous-match convention
rule: IndexOf("", start) = start, so IndexOf("") = 0.

title: StartsWith("") is true — the vacuous-match convention
rule: Empty needle (v0.230): Contains("") = true; StartsWith("") = true; EndsWith("") = true.

title: PadCenter puts the odd extra padding character on the right
rule: PadCenter splits the padding evenly; when it is odd, the extra character goes to the RIGHT: "ab".PadCenter(5) = " ab  ".

title: IsNullOrWhiteSpace(null) is true
rule: static pure method IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value: string?): bool;

title: GetEnumerator on an open-ended range raises InvalidOperationException
rule: Calling GetEnumerator on an open-ended range (IsOpenEnded is true) raises InvalidOperationException.

title: IsEmpty is true for an empty exclusive-bound range
rule: public pure readonly property IsEmpty: bool; // true if the range contains no values

title: FromUnderlyingOrNull returns null for an undeclared underlying value
rule: It returns the declared constant whose underlying value equals value, or null when there is none — total, never raises.

title: NameOf returns the declared constant's own identifier
rule: NameOf(value) returns the constant's identifier — under duplicate values, the first-declared constant's; the pair round-trips up to aliasing.

title: IntPtr's explicitly-declared equality compares by address
rule: Equality for these types is therefore declared explicitly ... the = and <> overloads plus the Equals(T) and override GetHashCode that language spec §25.2's co-declaration rule requires.

title: CString.Length is the byte length excluding the null terminator
rule: public readonly property Length: int; // byte length, excluding the null terminator

title: CString has no public constructor — instances come from its factory methods
rule: public class CString // No public constructor; obtained via factory methods.

title: CString.From(s) is the sanctioned construction route
rule: public static method From(s: string): owned CString;

title: RawBytes.From copies the source buffer; later mutation does not affect it
rule: RawBytes.From(buffer) allocates a fresh, owned RawBytes containing a copy of the source bytes. Mutations to the source after construction do not affect the RawBytes; the buffer is independent.

title: CopyTo writes Length bytes starting at destOffset
rule: CopyTo(destination, destOffset) // copies Length bytes into destination[destOffset .. destOffset+Length).

title: a CopyTo window outside the destination's Count raises IndexOutOfRangeException
rule: a window outside destination's Count raises IndexOutOfRangeException (the §1/§7.1 window rule).

title: RawBytes is not sendable and cannot cross a domain boundary
rule: RawBytes is a class and not sendable (language spec §30.14's class rule — not sealed), so a FromForeign view never crosses a domain boundary; stated here so the invariant is explicit.

title: Ptr<T>.Zero compares equal to itself under the intrinsic address equality
rule: public static readonly property Zero: Ptr<T>; ... The intrinsic compares the address representation.

title: Ptr<Ptr<T>> nested pointer is not admitted
rule: Nested Ptr<Ptr<T>> is NOT admitted (language spec §32.12).

title: a single-level Ptr<T> over an admitted pointee type is admitted
rule: T is gated (per-instantiation ...) to the FFI-POINTEE SET: integer types, float, double, bool, IntPtr, UIntPtr, and C-compatible records.

title: Interop.CodeAddress accepts a capture-free static method reference
rule: F gated per-instantiation to FFI-compatible function types ... a static method reference or a non-capturing lambda.

title: Interop.CodeAddress rejects a capturing lambda argument
rule: a capture-bearing argument is rejected with §32.8's diagnostic; the env clause does not apply.
